LuaJIT FrameWork Reference

LuaJIT 2.1 · Windows x64

Setup and usage

If your script is beside this reference in the extracted directory, add this line before the example code:

dofile("FrameWork/setup_paths.lua")

Run the script from that directory or pass the absolute path to setup_paths.lua. Load a module with require("module_name").

  • Square brackets in signatures mark optional arguments. Omit the brackets in calls.
  • Pass text and paths to FrameWork as UTF-8. Binary APIs use Lua strings as byte sequences.
  • Check each function's return values. An empty string, 0, false, or nil without a message can be a valid result.
  • Examples that use != require a LuaJIT build that supports this operator.

Error handling and special return values

Error handling

Return values, failures, and exceptions

Read the Returns and Error handling sections for the specific function or object method. A common return on handled failure is nil, message[, code].

message is a diagnostic string. code is an optional subsystem error code. Argument validation and some legacy wrappers may return only a message, even after a Windows API failure. Use a separate code when available for programmatic checks.

SituationHow to interpret the result
Operation failureSee the function's contract. Typically result == nil and message is a string.
Missing object, selection, or line, EOF, or a canceled dialogSome APIs return nil without a message in these cases. At EOF, file:Read returns an empty string and reader:Next returns nil without a message.
IPC or sync timeout, no event, or a file range in useThese cases can return false as a normal result. MutexLock returns true, "abandoned" when it acquires an abandoned mutex.
process.RunWait / ExecWaitWith nil, "timeout", pid, the third result is the process ID. Other failures may return a system error code there.
str.IsValidUtf8 / encoding.IsValidUtf8An invalid string returns false, bytePosition, message. An invalid type returns nil and a message.
HTTP 4xx or 5xxReturns a response table with the HTTP status. Download leaves the destination file untouched for these responses.
Reading diagnosticsgui.ErrorGet and l_vars.ErrorGet return the saved message as the first result.

File operation example

local fs = require("fs")
local bytes, message, code = fs.FileReadBytes("D:\\temp\\data.bin", 1024)
if bytes == nil then
    print(message, code)
    return
end
print(#bytes) -- zero is valid for an empty file or EOF

Callbacks and asynchronous error reporting

An exception in the callback for timer.Poll, fs.DirWalk, fs.FileCopyProgress, fs.Watch():Poll, clipboard.OnChange():Poll, audio.OnDeviceChange():Poll, tray.Poll, or http.Download onProgress returns nil, nonempty error message, 31. This includes thrown objects whose __tostring raises an error. To cancel normally, use the callback return value specified by the function.

The GUI reports callback exceptions to the handler set by gui.ErrorHandlerSet and makes the latest message available through gui.ErrorGet. OnClick and OnChange return when registration finishes. ipc.CommandListen reports callback errors to stderr. Clipboard callbacks dispatched by the window procedure also report errors to stderr. An explicit Poll returns the error to its caller.

When functions raise exceptions

The legacy fs.FileReadLine and its iterator raise errors on open, read, or close. This keeps a failure distinct from EOF in a for loop. To handle errors through return values, use fs.FileLinesOpen and check each reader:Next() call. Direct assignment to a protected l_vars.L_* field raises a metamethod error. l_vars.Set returns the error.

Public str functions catch type, UTF-8, index, and format validation errors and return error values. Most GUI functions also catch validation exceptions. WndProc is a low-level handler.

Errors during require, FFI calls, memory allocation, and user metamethods can still raise exceptions. This also applies to unsupported platforms and incorrect low-level calls. An invalid FFI pointer can terminate the process.

Error code spaces

Win32, WinHTTP, HRESULT, NTSTATUS, SQLite, GDI+, MCI, and PowerShell exit codes are separate code spaces. Articles identify which one applies. For example, callback code 31 belongs to a different space than SQLite codes. An unsigned positive HRESULT from OpenWith and the same bits interpreted as a signed negative HRESULT by another COM API require conversion before comparison. Windows can return codes beyond the examples in this reference.

Resource cleanup and partial operations

Check the results of Close and Flush separately from Write. Preserve the initial error if cleanup also fails. Each method documents whether you can close a resource again. The reference covers files, streams, subscriptions, speech, audio, SQLite, images, and tray objects. Keep the original self and internal object fields intact.

Recursive operations and writes can make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback depends on the operation. Download writes to a temporary file and publishes it after a successful download.

Getting started

setup_paths – Connecting the Library 1
setup_paths – Connecting modules
dofile("FrameWork/setup_paths.lua")
Purpose

Connect the Framework from a Lua file without configuring the LuaJIT paths.

Description

Run with dofile. It prepends the library directory to package.path and package.cpath and returns the directory path. The standard io and os libraries are still available.

Parameters
path
Path to setup_paths.lua. The relative path in the example is resolved against the current working directory.
Returns

Returns the FrameWork directory path as a string and updates the module search paths. Subsequent require failures still raise errors.

Error handling

Calling this code from anything other than a file triggers an assertion. Lua and required dependency errors during loading still raise exceptions.

Example

local dir = dofile("FrameWork/setup_paths.lua")
local str = require("str")
print(dir, str.Len("Привет"))
App - Application paths and working directory 10
app.L_ScriptPath
app.L_ScriptPath
Purpose

Find out the full path of the main script.

Description

Stores the absolute path calculated during the first require("app") or installation via ScriptPathSet.

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Absolute UTF-8 path of Lua script from arg[0].

Error handling

The table field itself does not return message/code. If initialization fails, use app.GetInfo(): it returns nil, message[, code]. For re-initialization, app.ScriptPathSet(). The path value is remembered when you load the module or call ScriptPathSet; changing the working directory does not change it. Assigning the field does not change the working directory Windows.

Example

local rt = require('app')
print(rt.L_ScriptPath)
app.L_ScriptDir
app.L_ScriptDir

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Lua script folder, not CWD.

Error handling

The table field itself does not return message/code. If initialization fails, use app.GetInfo(): it returns nil, message[, code]. For re-initialization, app.ScriptPathSet(). The path value is remembered when you load the module or call ScriptPathSet; changing the working directory does not change it. Assigning the field does not change the working directory Windows.

Example

local rt = require('app')
print(rt.L_ScriptDir)
app.L_ScriptName
app.L_ScriptName

Find out the name of the main script without a path.

Description

Stores the last component of the absolute path of the script along with the extension.

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

String. The last component of the script path.

Error handling

The table field itself does not return message/code. If initialization fails, use app.GetInfo(): it returns nil, message[, code]. For re-initialization, app.ScriptPathSet(). The path value is remembered when you load the module or call ScriptPathSet; changing the working directory does not change it. Assigning the field does not change the working directory Windows.

Example

local rt = require('app')
print(rt.L_ScriptName)
app.L_WorkingDir
app.L_WorkingDir
Purpose

Read the current working directory through the module field.

Description

Each time it reads, it requests the current Windows working directory.

The current Windows working directory in UTF-8. The field reads it from Windows on each access, including after fs.CurrentDirSet. Call app.WorkingDirGet() to get error details. Call app.WorkingDirSet(path) to change it. Assigning the field does not change the working directory.

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Returns the UTF-8 path string.

Error handling

If Windows fails, the field is equal to nil. For text and error code, call app.WorkingDirGet().

Example

local app = require("app")
local folder = app.L_WorkingDir
if folder == nil then
    local _, err, code = app.WorkingDirGet()
    print(err, code)
    return
end
print(folder)
app - launch paths
require("app")
Purpose

Connect the module to work with the script path and the working directory.

Description

Connection: local app = require("app"). The module determines the full path of the main script, its folder and name. The current working directory reads from Windows; it may differ from the script folder.

GetInfo returns a new path table. ScriptPathSet is only needed to explicitly specify the main script. WorkingDirSet changes the working directory of the entire process, and WorkingDirGet reads it. L_InitialWorkingDir saves the folder at the time of the first module load.

Parameters
module name
Pass the string "app" to Lua’s require function.
Returns

Table of the app module with functions and fields about paths.

Error handling

The download error depends on the demand and its dependencies. The script path error returns app.GetInfo().

Example

local app = require("app")
local info, err, code = app.GetInfo()
if not info then print(err, code); return end
print(info.L_ScriptDir)
print(info.L_WorkingDir)
app.WorkingDirSet
app.WorkingDirSet([path])
Purpose

Configure where the script will open files in relative ways.

Description

It changes the Windows working directory for the whole process, and then a relative path like data.txt is counted from the new folder, and without argument, it selects the main script folder, and the explicit path is transmitted by the UTF-8 string.

The fields L_ScriptPath, L_ScriptDir and L_ScriptName do not change. L_WorkingDir and WorkingDirGet immediately return the new current folder.

Parameters
path optional
The UTF-8 path to the catalogue. Without argument, app.L_ScriptDir is used.
Returns

true after successfully changing the working directory

Error handling

An empty path or an incorrect type is given by nil, message. If Windows fails, a third result of code is possible. Without an argument, the saved script path failure is transmitted if initialization fails.

Example

local app = require("app")
local original, err, code = app.WorkingDirGet()
if not original then print(err, code); return end
local ok, message, status = app.WorkingDirSet()
if not ok then print(message, status); return end
print(app.WorkingDirGet())
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = app.WorkingDirSet(original)
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
app.ScriptPathSet
app.ScriptPathSet([scriptPath])
Purpose

Explicitly specify the path of the main script when arg[0] is missing or points to the bootloader.

Description

Remembers the absolute path of the main script, its folder and name. The module automatically invokes this function at the first require("app") using arg[0]. In a normal .lua script, no re-calling is required.

An explicit call is needed to run from an application that did not transmit arg[0], or to select another main script. The relative path is allowed relative to the current working directory at the time of the call, the function does not run the script, does not verify the existence of the file, and does not change the working directory.

For the file right at the root of the disk, L_ScriptDir saves the final separator, including in the extended Windows path.

Parameters
scriptPath optional
The path of UTF-8 to the main script. If omitted, read arg[0]
Returns

true after L_ScriptPath, L_ScriptDir and L_ScriptName updates.

Error handling

In the absence of a suitable path or failure of its resolution — nil, message[, code].

Example

local app = require("app")
-- Usually require has already determined the path by arg[0].
-- A clear call is required if the launcher has not filled in the arg[0]
-- or you need to specify another main script:
local ok, err, code = app.ScriptPathSet("D:\\temp\\main.lua")
if not ok then print(err, code); return end
print(app.L_ScriptPath)
print(app.L_ScriptDir)
app.GetInfo
app.GetInfo()
Purpose

Get information about the launch and working directory in one table.

Description

Returns paths in one new table: L_ScriptPath is the full path of the script, L_ScriptDir is its folder, L_ScriptName is the file name, L_WorkingDir is the current working directory of Windows at the time of the call, which is convenient for checking initialization and searching for files next to the script.

The script folder and the working directory can be different: the relative file paths of Windows count from the working directory. The script paths are determined by ScriptPathSet, and the working directory is read anew with each GetInfo.

The resulting table does not update itself. To find out a new working directory, call GetInfo again or WorkingDirGet. Changing the fields of the resulting table does not change the app.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

New table with L_ScriptPath, L_ScriptDir, L_ScriptName and L_WorkingDir.

Error handling

Failure to initialize the script path or failure to read the working directory – nil, message[, code].

Example

local app = require("app")
local info, err, code = app.GetInfo()
if not info then print(err, code); return end
print("Скрипт:", info.L_ScriptPath)
print("Папка скрипта:", info.L_ScriptDir)
print("Имя скрипта:", info.L_ScriptName)
print("Рабочая папка:", info.L_WorkingDir)
-- For example, the settings file next to the script:
local configPath = info.L_ScriptDir .. "\\settings.ini"
print(configPath)
app.WorkingDirGet
app.WorkingDirGet()
Purpose

Find out which folder Windows allows process paths.

Description

Reads the current working directory directly from Windows. It does not require successful script path initialization.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

Returns the absolute path as a UTF-8 string.

Error handling

On Windows API failure, returns nil, message, code.

Example

local app = require("app")
local dir, err, code = app.WorkingDirGet()
if not dir then print(err, code); return end
print(dir)
app.L_InitialWorkingDir
app.L_InitialWorkingDir
Purpose

Find out which folder the process worked in when the app was first downloaded.

Description

Stores the working directory value obtained in the first require("app").

The working directory Windows at the first require("app"). The value is saved and does not change after WorkingDirSet or ScriptPathSet. If you read the error, the field is nil. For the current folder, use WorkingDirGet().

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Returns the initial path as a UTF-8 string.

Error handling

If you cannot get the current folder when downloading the app, the field is equal to nil. Additional values are not returned when reading the field.

Example

local app = require("app")
print(app.L_InitialWorkingDir)
argv – command line arguments 5
argv.At
argv.At(index)
Purpose

Get one argument of the original Windows command line by index.

Description

Argument on the index; negative indices are counted from the end.

Indexes begin at 1. Index 1 identifies the program. Script arguments begin at index 2.

Parameters
index
Integer index from 1, unless the function note says otherwise.
Returns

Argument line. The missing index is nil without a message. The wrong index is nil, message. Initial reading error is nil, message[, code].

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The command line and array are read when the module is loaded. The saved error is returned from the function: GetCommandLineW did not return the string, CommandLineToArgvW failure, WideCharToMultiByte conversion or LocalFree conversion. CommandLine returns the command line saved when the module was loaded; Get/Count/At/Program uses the array of arguments saved at the same time. The subsequent change to the global arg does not reread the Windows command line.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • The index of the argument should be a finite integer

Example

local argv = require('argv')
local result, err, code = argv.At(1)
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)
argv.CommandLine
argv.CommandLine()
Purpose

See how Windows transmitted the original command to the process.

Description

The original Windows command line in UTF-8.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

Returns a string or nil and an error message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The command line and array are read when the module is loaded. The saved error is returned from the function: GetCommandLineW did not return the string, CommandLineToArgvW failure, WideCharToMultiByte conversion or LocalFree conversion. CommandLine returns the command line saved when the module was loaded; Get/Count/At/Program uses the array of arguments saved at the same time. The subsequent change to the global arg does not reread the Windows command line.

Example

local argv = require('argv')
local result, err, code = argv.CommandLine()
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

single_instance – One instance of 1
single_instance - one copy
single_instance — один экземпляр
Purpose

Allow only one copy of the main script to work.

Description

One line at the beginning of the program is enough:

The application name and a separate function call are not required. Verification is done at the time of demand. The first process continues, the re-run of the same script is completed with code 0 until the next lines are executed. After the first process is completed, the startup is again allowed.

The module works separately from GUI and Framework. You need Windows 10/11 and LuaJIT with standard ffi. Additional DLL is not required: you use the system kernel32.dll and bcrypt.dll. Put single_instance.lua in the Lua search folder. When using the Framework, first configure the module search via setup_paths.lua, then perform the demand.

The key is automatically obtained from the full path of the main script running arg[0]. Relative paths are converted to absolute, short names 8.3 are disclosed, the register is normalized by Windows. Command-line arguments do not change the key. The same script cannot be run a second time; other scripts and copies in other folders can work simultaneously. The content of the file is not involved in the key: editing the script does not remove the limitation of the already working process.

Place require at the beginning of the program, before changing CWD or arg[0]. If there is no script running (mode -e, stdin or built-in host without arg[0]), the EXE path is used. Such launches with one EXE share the limitation. Arbitrary aliases via junction/symlink are not combined into a single key. The restriction applies in the current Windows session.

No need to save the result: Lua holds it in package.loaded. Repeated requires uses the cache in the same process and does not create a new HANDLE. Do not manually unload the module from package.loaded and call its result as a function. No global variables are added.

At the end of the process, including the emergency, Windows closes HANDLE. Closing one GUI window does not remove the restriction by itself while the process is running. Lock files are not created. The second process does not activate the window of the first.

If an application path cannot be determined or WinAPI returns an error, require causes a Lua error. The error is not considered permission to restart. You can use pcall(require, "single_instance") to process the errors.

Example: Lesson 34 shows how to re-start and remove the restriction after the first process has been completed. In a HTML builder, turn on "Disallow re-start" and add exactly the require("single_instance") string before downloading GUI.

CreateMutexW, GetFullPathNameW and BCryptHash are used.

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Opaque retained demand() token mutex (cdata) When repeated, the process is normally terminated via os.exit(0); management to the calling code is not returned.

Error handling

Cannot resolve, normalize, or hash the path, or cannot create the mutex: require(single_instance) raises a Lua error. A second instance exits the process, so it cannot wait for an error return.

Example

require("single_instance")
require("single_instance")

local gui = require("gui")
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = gui.WindowClient("Приложение", 480, 300, "fixed", "center")
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
gui.Run()

Purpose

Get a value by name and check for possible failure with one call.

Description

For example, Get("L_Year") reads a year, and Get("counter") reads a counter value. Unlike reading a property through a dot, Get allows you to get a value and an error message in a single call. The name can be stored in a variable.

name is a string with the exact name of a property or user field. Letter register is important.

Parameters
name
The string name of the built-in property or user field.
Returns

Built-in or custom value: An unknown name gives nil without a message.

Error handling

An incorrect name type or failure to calculate a property gives nil, message[, code]. Get itself does not record an error for ErrorGet.

Example

local vars = require("l_vars")
local name = "L_Year"
local value, message, code = vars.Get(name)
if message then
    print("Ошибка:", message, code)
elseif value == nil then
    print("Такого свойства нет:", name)
else
    print(value) -- Example: 2026
end

print(vars.L_Year) -- A simple reading returns only the value.
l_vars.ErrorGet
l_vars.ErrorGet()
Purpose

Read the diagnosis after referring to the computed property through a point.

Description

Returns the last-read error of the computed property through a point, such as vars.L_Month. This read returns only the value, so the error message can be received by a separate ErrorGet call.

Call ErrorGet as soon as you want to read it: the next reading of the built-in property will replace the saved diagnostics. Successful reading of the built-in property clears the previous error. Reading the existing user field does not calculate the built-in property or update the diagnostics.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

message, code saved error, or nil, nil. Reading saves the record.

Error handling

Takes into account the result of the last read of the built-in property through the dot. Get and Set errors are returned by their calls directly.

Example

local vars = require("l_vars")
local month = vars.L_Month
local message, code = vars.ErrorGet() -- Right after reading.
if message then
    print("Не удалось получить месяц:", message, code)
else
    print(month)
end

-- Same result with one call, without ErrorGet:
local value, err, status = vars.Get("L_Month")
if err then print(err, status); return end
print(value)
l_vars.Set
l_vars.Set(name, value)
Purpose

Store the values used by different modules of the same program.

Description

Creates or updates a custom field in l_vars. For example, Set("counter", 10) stores a value you can read with Get("counter") or vars.counter. Use this for values shared across modules in one program.

Data is stored only in the memory of the current process: Set does not write it to a file, does not transfer it to another program, and does not store it after completion. Repeated require("l_vars") in the same environment Lua returns the same table.

name is a string with the user field name. Names starting with L_ are protected from writing. Do not use the Get, Set and ErrorGet function names: they can be erased. value is a stored value of Lua; nil deletes the field.

Parameters
name
The string name of the built-in property or user field.
value
Lua is a storage value. Pass nil to delete the field.
Returns

true after writing or deleting the user field.

Error handling

An incorrect name type or attempt to write a protected L_* gives nil, message. Set does not update the diagnostics for ErrorGet.

Example

local vars = require("l_vars")
local ok, message = vars.Set("counter", 10)
if not ok then print(message); return end

print(vars.Get("counter")) -- 10
print(vars.counter)        -- 10

local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = vars.Set("counter", 20)
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
print(vars.counter)        -- 20

local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = vars.Set("counter", nil) -- Field removal.
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
print(vars.Get("counter"))       -- nil

local saved, reason = vars.Set("L_Year", "2000")
print(saved, reason) -- nil and message: built-in property cannot be changed.

GUI windows and controls

gui - windows and controls - WinAPI 109
gui.Button
gui.Button(nId, [cText], [nX], [nY], nWidth, nHeight)
Purpose

Create a regular button.

Description

Create a regular button.

ID is a unique integer of 1..65535 and the returned HWND is valid until the control/window is destroyed.

Parameters
nId
Unique string name of an existing control. Low-level calls also accept internal numeric IDs.
cText optional
Line: For API text, UTF-8; the default purpose/value is specified in the function description. Default: is empty text.
nX optional
Number of coordinate/size/shift: Units defined by the module: GUI logical, window/mouse screen pixels. Default: 0.
nY optional
Number of coordinate/size/shift: Units defined by the module: GUI logical, window/mouse screen pixels. Default: 0.
nWidth
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
nHeight
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
Returns

HWND cdata or nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CreateWindowExW failed (Win32 error
  • Failed to position GroupBox behind controls
  • GUI window is not created
  • MultiByteToWideChar failed
  • OleScriptPathSet failed for drag-and-drop (HRESULT
  • RegisterDragDrop failed (HRESULT
  • SetDialogControlDpiChangeBehavior failed
  • SetWindowSubclass failed for GroupBox background
  • control ID is already in use
  • control ID must be an integer from 1 to 65535
  • control dimensions must be nonnegative numbers
  • drop target window is not available
  • invalid UTF-8 text
  • logical coordinate must be a finite number within +/-10000000
  • text contains NUL character

Example

local g = require('gui')
local hwnd, sampleError, sampleCode = g.Window('Пример', 500, 280, "fixed")

Creates HFONT for low-level WinAPI. Use gui.FontSet(id,name,size,bold,italic) for the control font.

The size in points is required and must be a finite number greater than 0 and at most 10000. With nil for the font family, Windows selects it automatically. Weight accepts "bold" or "normal" and style accepts "italic" or "normal". Both default to "normal".

Result: HFONT or nil, error. The font is owned by the library. Do not pass the descriptor to native FontSet. FontsDelete is called after closing the font-using windows.

When skipping: nil - Windows selects the headset by font parameters.

We need to pass on the meaning.

gui.HandlerDispatch
gui.HandlerDispatch(aHandlers, nId)
Purpose

Call the handler from the transmitted table.

Description

Call the handler from the transmitted table.

Internal helper: The handler error is intercepted and written in stderr; the line name is allowed in _G.

Parameters
aHandlers
Lua-table for storing processors by ID.
nId
Unique string name of an existing control. Low-level calls also accept internal numeric IDs.
Returns

1 if successfully delivered to an existing processor; 0 if there is no processor or the delivery of the processor ended in an error; the wrong type of handler table is nil, message. The error of the handler itself is transmitted via ErrorHandlerSet/ErrorGet.

Error handling

The incorrect handler table is nil, message. The missing or failed handler is 0; the details of the callback error go to gui.ErrorHandlerSet/ErrorGet. Don't check the result only as boolean: 0 in Lua is true.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

  • GUI handler error:
  • GUI handler must be a function or global function name\n
  • GUI handler not found:
  • handlers must be a table

Example

local g = require('gui')
local hwnd, sampleError, sampleCode = g.Window('Пример', 500, 280, "fixed")
if not hwnd then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end

gui.TextColorSet
gui.TextColorSet(nId, [color]) / gui.TextColorSet(nId, red, green, blue)
Purpose

Set your own text color for supported control.

Description

TextColorSet(id, color) and TextColorSet(id, red, green, blue) set the text color of an existing Label. The color can be a case-insensitive name such as "Red", "Blue", or "Green", an integer from 0 to 0xFFFFFF in 0xRRGGBB format, a #RRGGBB string, a 0x string with 1 to 6 hex digits, or a decimal string. Leading and trailing whitespace in strings is ignored. The three-integer RGB form still accepts components from 0 to 255. TextColorSet(id, nil) or TextColorSet(id) restores the system text color. Returns true on success or nil and an error message. Invalid colors and other control types are rejected without changing the color. Green is 0x008000 and Lime is 0x00FF00. A single numeric color uses RRGGBB. The WinAPI COLORREF format uses BBGGRR.

Call these functions after creating the Label. Quote color names. "Red", "RED", and "red" are equivalent. The decimal value 16711680 and 0xFF0000 both mean red. 0x0000FF is blue, and the three components 255, 0, 0 mean red. Numeric colors have no alpha channel. Pass nil to reset the color. "Default" is not a valid color name.

Name. RGB
Black #000000
White #FFFFFF
Red #FF0000
Green #008000
Lime #00FF00
Blue #0000FF
Yellow #FFFF00
Cyan #00FFFF
Aqua #00FFFF
Magenta #FF00FF
Fuchsia #FF00FF
Gray #808080
Grey #808080
Silver #C0C0C0
Maroon #800000
Olive #808000
Navy #000080
Teal #008080
Purple #800080
Orange #FFA500
Pink #FFC0CB
Brown #A52A2A
Gold #FFD700
Darkgray #A9A9A9
Darkgrey #A9A9A9
Lightgray #D3D3D3
Lightgrey #D3D3D3
Darkred #8B0000
Darkgreen #006400
Darkblue #00008B

This is a list of 30 names, not all of them CSS. The values are w3C palette. Green is dark green; bright green is Lime.

The method is only for gui.Label. Button, Edit, CheckBox, RadioButton, GroupBox and arbitrary ControlCreate are rejected. Background and font are saved. TextSet, FontSet, moving, redrawing and changing DPI retain color. Once the window is closed or Label removed, the color is cleared. No new GDI brushes and no individual handlers are created for each Label.

The Label Text Color tutorial shows color names, one-number colors, and the three-component RGB form. In the designer, select a Label and enable "Custom text color." Enter a name such as Red, an integer such as 16711680 or 0xFF0000, or a #RRGGBB string, or choose a color in the palette. The preview and JSON use the same names and numbers. Export retains the selected representation. Existing JSON with #RRGGBB and calls to TextColorSet(id, r, g, b) continue to work.

Parameters
nId
We need to pass on the meaning.
color optional
If you skip: nil - reset the color of the Label text to the system. In the RGB variant, all three components are mandatory.
red
We need to pass on the meaning.
green
We need to pass on the meaning.
blue
We need to pass on the meaning.
Returns

true for success. Failure: nil, message.

gui.Label
gui.Label(nId, [cText], [nX], [nY], nWidth, nHeight, [cAlign], [cVAlign])
Purpose

Use a unique string name for control.

Description

Optional cAlign: "left", "center", "right"; cVAlign: "top", "center".

Use the unique string name of the control. The returned HWND is valid until the control/window is destroyed.

In the native gui module, a regular Label already supports several lines. There is no need for a separate function or flag.

  • For an explicit transition to the next line, transfer \r\n inside the Lua line.
  • Long text is automatically transferred to words within nWidth. One word without spaces that is wider than control can be cropped.
  • The nHeight is manually set: Label does not automatically increase the height or show the scroll bar. If the height is not high enough, the bottom rows are cropped.
  • Dimensions are logical units 96 DPI. Consider the number of lines, the font chosen, and additional width transfers.

Transfer in width without obvious transitions:

Changing the text saves the size of the Label. After enlarging the text, check if it is high enough:

Label displays text. Use gui.EditMulti to type and edit a few lines.

The basis of native Label behavior: Win32 SS_LEFT; microsoft style.

Dimensions are given in logical units 96 DPI. Choose the height based on the number of lines, the selected font and possible width transfers.

Parameters
nId
Unique string name of an existing control. Low-level calls also accept internal numeric IDs.
cText optional
Line: For API text, UTF-8; the default purpose/value is specified in the function description. Default: is empty text.
nX optional
Number of coordinate/size/shift: Units defined by the module: GUI logical, window/mouse screen pixels. Default: 0.
nY optional
Number of coordinate/size/shift: Units defined by the module: GUI logical, window/mouse screen pixels. Default: 0.
nWidth
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
nHeight
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
cAlign optional
At skip: Alignment on the left edge.
cVAlign optional
When skipping: Alignment on the upper edge.
Returns

HWND cdata or nil, message.

gui.MessageBox
gui.MessageBox([cText], [cTitle], [buttons], [icon], [defaultButton])
Purpose

Use to report an error or get a user’s decision.

Description

Shows a dialogue with a message and buttons. Use to report an error or get a user's decision.

Native gui shows the standard Windows modal window. The text and header is UTF-8. The result is the numerical ID of the pressed button; if it is mistaken, nil, error. The owner is the main GUI window, if it is created. You can call without the main window.

As before: one OK button and an information icon. All new options are optional.

buttons Buttons Possible results
"ok" OK gui.Answer.Ok
"ok-cancel" OK, Cancellation gui.Answer.Ok, gui.Answer.Cancel
"yes-no" Yeah, no. gui.Answer.Yes, gui.Answer.No
"yes-no-cancel" Yeah, no, cancellation. gui.Answer.Yes, gui.Answer.No, gui.Answer.Cancel
"retry-cancel" Repeat, Cancel. gui.Answer.Retry, gui.Answer.Cancel
"abort-retry-ignore" Interrupt, Repeat, Miss gui.Answer.Abort, gui.Answer.Retry, gui.Answer.Ignore
"cancel-try-continue" Cancel, Repeat, Continue gui.Answer.Cancel, gui.Answer.TryAgain, gui.Answer.Continue

The default is "ok." Button names are localized by Windows. These are ready-made system sets: arbitrary signatures and an arbitrary number of buttons MessageBoxW does not support.

icon species
"information" Information; by default
"warning" Warning
"error" Mistake
"question" Question
"none" No icons.

The buttons and icon values are the exact strings in the lower case. Unknown strings, numbers and logical values return nil, error without showing the window.

The optional fifth defaultButton argument is the sequence number of the button from 1 to the number of buttons of the selected set. The default is 1. This is the position from left to right, not the ID of the result.

Enter presses the current selected button. Escape returns gui.Answer.Cancel if there is a Cancellation in the set; for one OK returns gui.Answer.Ok. For a set without OK and Cancellations, Escape does not close the window.

When MessageBox is called from the button handler or menu, it automatically appears in the center of the native GUI main window, including its frame and header. No additional parameter is needed. If precise centering would bring the message window out of the monitor workspace, the position shifts into the available area. Without the main window, the position selects Windows.

After moving the main window, the next message is centered on its new position. Returnable ID buttons and buttons/icon/defaultButton settings are unchanged.

Parameters
cText optional
When omitted, "" is an empty text.
cTitle optional
When omitted, "" is an empty headline.
buttons optional
Pass: "ok."
icon optional
Pass: "Information."
defaultButton optional
On pass: 1.
Returns

The numerical ID of the pressed button. If you make an error, nil, message.

Understandable names are available immediately after local gui = require("gui"). Do not connect win_constants to compare the result. These are numerical constants: for example, gui.Answer.Yes = 6, gui.Answer.No = 7. The former numerical ID and ffi.C.ID* remain compatible. Retry and TryAgain (Repeat) are different results of different sets of buttons.

ID Constant gui Button
1 gui.Answer.Ok OK
2 gui.Answer.Cancel Cancellation
3 gui.Answer.Abort Interrupt.
4 gui.Answer.Retry Repeat.
5 gui.Answer.Ignore Let go.
6 gui.Answer.Yes Yes.
7 gui.Answer.No No.
10 gui.Answer.TryAgain Repeat.
11 gui.Answer.Continue Continue.

Compare ID to the desired value: any non-zero number, including No and Cancellation, is considered true in Lua. The assert call (gui.MessageBox(...)) only checks the absence of error, not the consent of the user. You do not need to create the main window again to show the message.

A full interactive example is the MessageBox Buttons and Icons lesson. Lesson 35 repeats this theme; lesson 26 shows confirmation from the menu.

Compatibility of sets, icons and results: Microsoft MessageBoxW.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Could not center the MessageBox on its owner
  • Could not determine the owner monitor work area
  • Could not measure the MessageBox or its owner
  • Could not remove the previous MessageBox positioning hook
  • MessageBox default button must be an integer from 1 to
  • MessageBoxW failed (Win32 error
  • MultiByteToWideChar failed
  • SetWindowsHookExW failed for MessageBox positioning
  • UnhookWindowsHookEx failed after MessageBox
  • WideCharToMultiByte failed
  • invalid UTF-8 text
  • text contains NUL character
  • unknown MessageBox button set
  • unknown MessageBox icon

Example

gui.MessageBox(text, title, buttons, icon, defaultButton)
gui.MessageBox("Готово", "Сообщение")
-- The second button (No) is selected by default:
local answer, err = gui.MessageBox("Продолжить?", "Подтверждение", "yes-no", "question", 2)
if answer == nil then error(err) end

if answer == gui.Answer.Yes then
    print("Выбрано Да")
elseif answer == gui.Answer.No then
    print("Выбрано Нет")
end
gui.MessageBox("File not found", "Ошибка", "ok", "error")
gui.MessageBox("Проверьте введённые данные", "Предупреждение", "ok-cancel", "warning")
gui.MessageBox("Operation completed", "Готово", "ok", "none")
local answer, err = gui.MessageBox("Повторить операцию?", "Операция", "retry-cancel", "warning", 2)
gui.OnClick("messageButton", function()
    gui.MessageBox("Сообщение по центру этого окна", "Сообщение", "ok", "information")
end)

gui.OnDropFiles
gui.OnDropFiles([nIdOrHandler], [cHandlerName])
Purpose

Assign a file drop handler for window or control.

Description

Assign a file drop handler for window or control.

Forms: OnDropFiles(handler) - window and inheritance; OnDropFiles(id,handler) - control. handler(paths) gets an array of UTF-8-paths. nil for control means to inherit, false - to prohibit; nil for the window removes the overall handler. Used OLE IDropTarget. To show the end of the long path in Edit, use gui.TextEndSet(id, paths[1]).

Parameters
nIdOrHandler optional
Overload: whole ID control or handler shared drop window; see both call forms. Default: nil - remove the common window handler.
cHandlerName optional
Callback function, the string name of the global function or nil. For drop control also false. Default: When calling with ID control: nil - inherit the window handler; false - disallow file reception. For named control, transmit the second argument explicitly, even if it is nil.
Returns

Returns true, or nil and an error message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • OleScriptPathSet failed for drag-and-drop (HRESULT
  • OnDropFiles: control does not exist
  • RegisterDragDrop failed (HRESULT
  • RevokeDragDrop failed (HRESULT
  • drop target window is not available
  • handler must be a function, global name or nil
  • handler must be a function, global name, nil (inherit), or false (disable)

Example

local g = require('gui')
local hwnd, sampleError, sampleCode = g.Window('Пример', 500, 280, "fixed")
if not hwnd then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = g.Edit("edit1",'Перетащите файлы',20,20,300,26)
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = g.OnDropFiles("edit1",function(paths)
    for _,path in ipairs(paths) do print(path) end
end)
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end
g.Run()

Purpose

Select an existing file.

Description

Select an existing file.

Native: title, filters={{name,mask},...}, initialDir. Several masks: *.lua;*.txt.

Parameters
cTitle optional
Line: For text API, UTF-8; the default destination/value is specified in the function description. Default: is an empty header.
filters optional
Native array {{{name, mask}, ...}; in file_dialog lies inside options.filters. Default: nil - without a file filter.
initialDir optional
UTF-8-path: The relative path is calculated from the current workflow folder. Default: nil is the default system folder for dialog.
Returns

The path to UTF-8; when canceled, nil; when mistaken, nil, err, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Expected UTF-8 string without NUL
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • filters must be a non-empty array of pairs {description, template}
  • initialDir should be an empty path to the folder
  • There should be no gaps in the filters array
  • For each filter, a non-empty description and template are needed.
  • dialog

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local gui = require('gui')
local result, err, code = gui.FileOpen('Открыть', {{'Текст', '*.txt'}})
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

gui.FontSet
gui.FontSet(nId, cFontName, nSize, [nBold], [nItalic])
Purpose

Assign a separate font to one control.

Description

Native gui.lua: FontSet(id, name, size, bold, italic) creates and assigns a typeface with one command, like DefaultFontSet.

Pass an existing control name, a UTF-8 font name, and a size in points. The size must be finite, greater than 0, and at most 10000. Weight and style default to "normal". Boolean and numeric style values are rejected.

The result is created by HFONT or nil, error; you don't need to save the result to a variable. The library stores the font and takes into account DPI. FontsDelete is called after the window is closed. FontSizeSet changes only the size, keeping the rest of the parameters.

The old native gui.FontSet(id, hfont) call is removed: replace the FontCreate/FontSet pair with one FontSet with name and size. FontCreate remains for low-level WinAPI. FontStyleSet is another name for FontSet.

The 35 lesson folders are named by topic without numerical names. All links and launch commands in the set are updated; main.lua and run.cmd remain inside the corresponding folder.

Parameters
nId
We need to pass on the meaning.
cFontName
We need to pass on the meaning.
nSize
We need to pass on the meaning.
nBold optional
When you pass, "normal."
nItalic optional
When you pass, "normal."
Returns

Descriptor of the assigned font HFONT. In case of error - nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

gui.TextEndSet
gui.TextEndSet(nId, [cText])
Purpose

Set text in a single-line Edit control and scroll horizontally to show the end of the text.

Description

Set text in a single-line Edit and scroll horizontally to show the end of a long line. The control keeps the full text.

See also: gui.TextSet(nId, cText) is the usual setting of text without special scrolling to the end of the line.

Uses TextSet, EM_SETSEL, and EM_SCROLLCARET; transfers the cursor to the end without highlighting. If the focus was on this Edit, it transfers it to the main window so that the cursor does not blink. If the focus is on another control, it does not change. The field remains editable. For multi-line Edit, horizontal scrolling is not guaranteed.

Example: Drag a folder from Explorer directly to Edit.

File ready: Examples/14_gui_set_text_end.lua.

cText: New text (UTF-8); Cyrillic and other Unicode characters are allowed. As in TextSet, nil is converted to an empty string.

Note: uses TextSet, EM_SETSEL and EM_SCROLLCARET. The cursor is set to the end of the text without highlighting. If the focus was on a given Edit, it is translated to the main window, the flashing cursor disappears. If the focus was on another control, it does not change. The field remains editable: clicking on it again allows you to enter text. For multi-line fields, horizontal scroll behavior is not guaranteed.

Parameters
nId
ID is an existing Edit single-line control (e.g., 102).
cText optional
New text (UTF-8), including Unicode; nil is converted to a blank line. Default: is empty text.
Returns

true on success; nil, message on error (e.g. unknown ID or invalid UTF-8).

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • MultiByteToWideChar failed
  • RevokeDragDrop failed (HRESULT
  • SetText failed
  • SetTextEnd: control does not exist
  • invalid UTF-8 text
  • text contains NUL character

Example

local g = require('gui')
local window, sampleError, sampleCode = g.Window('Путь к проекту', 500, 160, "fixed")
if not window then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = g.Edit("edit1", '', 20, 25, 445, 26)
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end

local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = g.OnDropFiles("edit1", function(paths)
    if paths[1] then
        local sampleValue4, sampleError4, sampleCode4 = g.TextEndSet("edit1", paths[1])
        if not sampleValue4 then print(sampleError4 or "Operation failed", sampleCode4); return end
    end
end)
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end

-- It also works with the usual software installation of text:
local sampleValue5, sampleError5, sampleCode5 = g.TextEndSet("edit1", 'C:\\Проекты 文 日本\\Очень длинная папка\\MyProject')
if not sampleValue5 then print(sampleError5 or "Operation failed", sampleCode5); return end

g.Run()

gui.Window
gui.Window([cTitle], nWidth, nHeight, [resizable], [position], [nY], [clientSize])
Purpose

Create a single main GUI window.

Description

Window takes the outer window size, including the frame and title bar. WindowClient takes the size of the client area that contains the controls. Both use logical units at 96 DPI. For example, 640 × 420 at 125% scaling is 800 × 525 physical pixels. WindowClient and MenuSet account for the menu. center=true or "center" centers the window. "bottom-left" puts it at the lower-left corner of the primary monitor work area. false or nil keeps the initial position. Numeric x and y are physical screen coordinates. Returns an HWND or nil and an error message. Sizes must be positive and within Windows limits.

Create a single main GUI window.

Repeat window until the first window closes is prohibited. Dimensions >0. resizable="resizable" allows you to resize, "fixed" fixes the size.

resizable: Native gui - "resizable" or "fixed"; by default "resizable." Logical and numerical values are not accepted.

Parameters
cTitle optional
Line: For text API, UTF-8; the default destination/value is specified in the function description. Default: is an empty header.
nWidth
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
nHeight
Numeric coordinate, size, or offset. The module determines the units. GUI uses logical units, while the window and mouse modules use screen pixels.
resizable optional
Native gui: "resizable" or "fixed"; default "resizable." Default: "resizable."
position optional
Native: "center", "bottom-left" or former boolean centering; in the presence of nY, this argument is treated as an on-screen X-coordinate. Default: nil is the original position of the window.
nY optional
Coordinate/size/shift number: Units are defined by the module: GUI logical, window/mouse screen pixels. Default: nil - do not set the pair X,Y. When you explicitly specify X through position, Y is required.
clientSize optional
When omitted: false - dimensions refer to the entire window; true - to the client area.
Returns

HWND cdata or nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Purpose

Use to calculate the free space when placing the window.

Description

Measures the height of the main taskbar Windows. Use to calculate the free space when placing the window.

Returns the height of the main system taskbar in physical pixels. For the top/bottom edge, the actual height, including auto-hide mode; for the left/right edge, 0. Requested via SHAppBarMessage(ABM_GETTASKBARPOS); if Windows does not provide data, nil, error returns. Do not replace the error with zero. The function does not calculate the full workspace and does not take into account third-party panels: for the position of the window, use "bottom-left".

Changes the font size of the item in paragraphs, retaining the rest of the properties.

Purpose

Intercept errors of GUI handlers for journal or own diagnostics.

Description

Registers the handler function (message, context) for event handler errors and internal callbacks GUI. Returns true or nil, err if the parameter is incorrect. nil disables delivery. The syntax of existing OnClick/OnClose/OnDropFiles is stored. MessageBox and stderr are not automatically used.

Parameters
handler
A function with the signature handler(message, context). Pass nil to disable the custom handler.
Returns

true after installing the function or disabling through nil. The incorrect type is nil, message. Returns of the registered handler are not the result of this call.

Error handling

The logger error itself is intercepted, re-entry does not cause recursive delivery. The last diagnosis remains in ErrorGet; reporter_error contains a logger error. Don't cause prolonged work in this handler.

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Most public GUI functions catch validation exceptions and return nil and an error message. Win32 error codes depend on the operation. Use ErrorHandlerSet and ErrorGet for event errors, which are reported when the event handler runs.

    print(context, message)
end

local ok, err = gui.ErrorHandlerSet(ReportGuiError)
if not ok then print(err); return end
-- Create a window and register handlers in the usual way.

Purpose

Reads the record of the last GUI exception. When true, clear deletes the record after reading.

true clears the saved diagnosis after reading.

message, context, sequence, reporter_error. If there is no record, the function does not return values.

Reads the diagnostics stored by the GUI subsystem. reporter_error contains an error of the user's diagnostic processor itself, if it occurs.

Example

local gui = require("gui")

end

Purpose

true is only allowed in the agreed destruction lifecycle of HWND. Default: false is allowed to check that the window has already been destroyed.

true after cleaning, with nil/NULL and if its icons are not; false if the window still exists and destroying is not specified. Wrong type/value HWND - nil, message.

source=nil means resource 1 of the current EXE; number 1..65535 is ID of the resource; line is UTF-8-path ICO relative to CWD. Usually use g.IconSet to allow GUI to automatically release the icons.

Parameters
hwnd
The current HWND cdata; the main HWND is derived from Window.
source optional
nil - resource ICO 1 current EXE; integer 1..65535 - ID resource; string - UTF-8-path ICO. Default: 1 - resource ICO current EXE.
Returns

Returns true, or nil and an error message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • GUI window does not exist
  • LoadImageW (large icon)
  • LoadImageW (small icon)
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • icon path must be a non-empty UTF-8 string without NUL
  • icon resource ID must be an integer from 1 to 65535
  • icon source must be an ICO path or resource ID
  • invalid HWND type
  • invalid HWND value

Example

local app_icon = require('app_icon')
local result, err, code = app_icon.Set(hwnd, 'пример.ico')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

file_dialog - File Dialogues 3
file_dialog.Open
file_dialog.Open({title=…, owner=…, initialFolder=…, fileName=…, filters=…, filterIndex=…})
Purpose

Select one existing file.

Description

The signature reveals the fields of a single settings table. All fields and the table itself are optional. The sign ... denotes the value of the field; when you call, substitute your value or remove the field.

Selects one existing file.

All fields are optional.

Field.Type and meaning
titlestring: dialog header in UTF-8. nil is header Windows.
ownerHWND: numerical window descriptor or compatible FFI pointer. nil/0 - no window-owner.
initialFolderstring: path to the existing starter folder in UTF-8. nil - folder selection provided by Windows.
fileNamestring: the initial text of the file name field in UTF-8. nil - do not specify.
filterstable: array of filters {{"Text", "*.txt;*.log"}, {"All files", "*.*"}}. Also allowed elements {name="Text", pattern="*.txt"}. nil/{} - filters are not specified.
filterIndexnumber: entire index of the selected filter from 1 to #filters. It is counted and checked only with blank filters. nil - index is not set, choice is provided by Windows.

defaultExtension is only used in save; open ignores it.

Strings must be correct UTF-8 without NUL. Additional unknown fields are ignored.

Parameters
options optional
The only argument is the settings table. By default, nil, which corresponds to {}. The fields are transmitted within the table, not by individual positional arguments.
Returns

The path to the file in UTF-8 when selected; nil when canceled; nil, err, code when mistaken.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • IFileDialog.SetFileName
  • IFileDialog.SetFileTypeIndex
  • IFileDialog.SetFileTypes
  • IFileDialog.SetFolder
  • IFileDialog.SetOptions
  • IFileDialog.SetTitle
  • IFileDialog.Show

  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • SHCreateItemFromParsingName
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • The parameters of the dialogue should be a table.

Example

local dialog = require('file_dialog')
local result, err, code = dialog.Open({title = 'Открыть файл'})
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

str.CodePoint
str.CodePoint(text, [first_index], [last_index])
Purpose

Learn the numerical codes of one or more UTF-8 characters.

Description

Unicode numerical codes of the character range.

Returns two indexes. first_index=1 and last_index=first_index.

The string is checked in its entirety. The byte offset table is not created; the result is returned in multiple numbers, not an array.

For positive indices, one pass checks all the text and saves only the requested range. For one character, an array is not created. Negative indices require a predetermined length.

An invalid argument or UTF-8 error returns nil and an error message without a stack trace. Native error codes are preserved when available. For invalid content, IsValidUtf8 returns false, the byte position, and a description.

Parameters
text
String. Use UTF-8 with text APIs. See the function description for the meaning and default value.
first_index optional
Unicode code item index with 1, negative from the end; string.* and Lua positional captures have byte rules. Default: 1.
last_index optional
Unicode code item index with 1, negative at the end; string.* and Lua positional captures have byte rules. Default: first_index is one code point.
Returns

Multiple numbers; outside the nil range.

str.Format
str.Format(format_text, [...])
Purpose

Prepare a message or table with line alignment by the number of Unicode code points.

Description

Substitutes values by format specifiers. For %s, width and accuracy are counted at UTF-8 code points, and %c takes the Unicode code point. Numerical specifiers and %q handles string.format.

The width and accuracy of %s are measured by code points, not bytes or screen speakers. %c accepts Unicode. For conventional byte formatting, use string.format().

Parameters
format_text
A format string with plain text and specifiers, such as [%5s] or %d.
... optional
Values in the order of the specifiers. For %s, pass a string, for %c, the whole Unicode code. For %%, insert a percentage, and don't consume values.
Returns

A line with substituted and formatted values.

Error handling

Incorrect format or UTF-8, incompatible type, missing or redundant argument give nil, message.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • must be a string
  • the symbol code must be an integer
  • unicode
  • inadmissible % format specifier
  • lack of format arguments
  • format specifier
  • invalid UTF-8 at byte
  • unexpected end of string
  • too many arguments of format

Example

local str = require("str")

print(str.Format("[%5s]", "АБ"))     -- [AB]
print(str.Format("[%-5s]", "АБ"))    -- [AB]
print(str.Format("[%.3s]", "Привет")) -- [Present]
print(str.Format("%s %c: %d%%", "Метка", 0x65E5, 42)) -- Метка 日: 42%

local text, err = str.Format("%s %s", "один")
if text == nil then
    print(err)
end

str.LTrim
str.LTrim(text)
Purpose

Remove Unicode spaces on the left.

Description

Remove Unicode spaces on the left.

It handles only the right edges of the line and stops at the first impenetrable character. It supports all 25 Unicode White_Space characters. The gaps inside the line are saved. If there's nothing to cut, it returns the original line.

A complete UTF-8 check is not performed: the remaining bytes are saved unchanged. If necessary, check the input data separately through str.IsValidUtf8(text). The argument type check is saved. The search for boundaries depends on the number of spaces at the edges; creating a cropped string requires copying the result.

An invalid argument or UTF-8 error returns nil and an error message without a stack trace. Native error codes are preserved when available. For invalid content, IsValidUtf8 returns false, the byte position, and a description.

str.Normalize
str.Normalize(text, [form])
Purpose

Perform the Windows Normaliz.dll Unicode Normalization.

Description

Perform the Windows Normaliz.dll Unicode Normalization.

Form: NFC (default), NFD, NFKC, NFKD. This is not a transliteration or encoding fix.

NFC is the canonical composition; NFD is the canonical decomposition; NFKC is the compatible composition; NFKD is the compatible decomposition. There are no separate functions of nfc/nfd/nfkc/nfkd.

The correctness of UTF-8 is checked when converting WinAPI. In case of an error, an additional check saves the Lua error with the position of the damaged byte.

The order of checks: text type, normalization form, availability of DLL, empty line; then UTF-8 → UTF-16. Therefore, with both incorrect form and damaged UTF-8, the form error returns. In the acceptable form and available DLL, the damaged UTF-8 still causes the Lua error.

An invalid argument or UTF-8 error returns nil and an error message without a stack trace. Native error codes are preserved when available. For invalid content, IsValidUtf8 returns false, the byte position, and a description.

Parameters
text
String. Use UTF-8 with text APIs. See the function description for the meaning and default value.
form optional
NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD; by default NFC. Default: "NFC".
Returns

Line or nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The public str API reports type, index, format, and UTF-8 errors as nil and an error message. Internal calls to error() are caught. Lower, Upper, and Normalize may also return an available Win32 error code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • NormalizeString
  • NormalizeString: Buffer did not contain the result
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • Allowable forms of normalization: NFC, NFD, NFKC and NFKD
  • Normaliz.dll was not downloaded:
  • The line is too long to convert UTF-8
  • A UTF-8 string is required
  • The form of normalization should be a string

Example

local value, err, code = require('str').Normalize('пример', 'NFC')
if value == nil then print(err) else print(value) end
local s = require('str')
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = s.Normalize('é', 'NFD') == 'e' .. s.Char(0x301)
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = s.Normalize('ＡＢ', 'NFKC') == 'AB'
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = s.Normalize('ＡＢ', 'NFKD') == 'AB'
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end

str.RTrim
str.RTrim(text)
Purpose

Remove Unicode spaces on the right.

Description

Remove Unicode spaces on the right.

It handles only the right edges of the line and stops at the first impenetrable character. It supports all 25 Unicode White_Space characters. The gaps inside the line are saved. If there's nothing to cut, it returns the original line.

A complete UTF-8 check is not performed: the remaining bytes are saved unchanged. If necessary, check the input data separately through str.IsValidUtf8(text). The argument type check is saved. The search for boundaries depends on the number of spaces at the edges; creating a cropped string requires copying the result.

An invalid argument or UTF-8 error returns nil and an error message without a stack trace. Native error codes are preserved when available. For invalid content, IsValidUtf8 returns false, the byte position, and a description.

Source line in UTF-8.
max_length
A non-negative integer number of code points, including the suffix.
suffix optional
UTF-8 string. By default "..." For pruning without the suffix, pass "..."
Returns

The UTF-8 string is no longer than the max_length code points, and at the limit of 0 you get an empty string.

A negative or fractional limit, an unsuitable type, and a detected incorrect UTF-8 yield a nil, message.

local str = require("str")

print(str.Truncate("Длинная строка", 8, "...")) -- Long...

print(str.Truncate("Привет", 2, "конец"))      -- ko

    print(err)
end

Parameters
path

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • invalid drive path
  • path cannot be nil
  • path does not contain a drive letter
  • NUL bytes are not allowed in the string
  • A nonempty path is required
  • A UTF-8 string is required

Example

local fs = require('fs')
local d, sampleError, sampleCode = fs.DriveGet('C:/')

print(d.path,d.type,d.total,d.free)

fs.FileAppend
fs.FileAppend(path, content, [encoding], [allow_lossy])
Purpose

Add encrypted content to the end of the file.

Description

Add encrypted content to the end of the file.

Appending to an existing nonempty file does not insert a BOM in the middle. Explicit UTF-8-BOM rewrites an existing UTF-8 file without a BOM to include one. An incompatible existing BOM is rejected for Unicode encodings. For explicit ANSI/ACP, OEM/OEMCP, and legacy CPxxxx encodings, the initial bytes are treated as data even if they resemble a BOM. CP65001 and numeric 65001 mean UTF-8 and still validate the Unicode BOM.

Difference with fs.FileAppendLine: FileAppend does not insert a line separator. If the file contains abc, the addition of def gives abcdef. You can transfer multi-line text to the content; you need to specify the translations of the lines yourself.

Parameters
path
UTF-8 path. Relative paths are resolved against the process's current working directory.
content
Value/data for the operation; acceptable type and format are listed below.
encoding optional
nil/UTF-8, UTF-8-BOM, UTF-16LE/BE, BINARY, ANSI/ACP, OEM/OEMCP, CP1251/Windows-1251 or a numerical code page. Default: "UTF-8".
allow_lossy optional
boolean: false/nil prohibits irreversible substitution when encoding; true permits. Default: false prohibits loss-of-character conversion.
Returns

true or nil, message[,code].

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

  • CloseHandle
  • CreateDirectoryW
  • CreateFileW
  • CreateFileW (stat)
  • FlushFileBuffers
  • GetFileAttributesW
  • GetFileInformationByHandle
  • GetFullPathNameW
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • ReadFile
  • SetEndOfFile
  • SetFilePointerEx
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • WriteFile
  • content must be a string or number
  • encoding mismatch: existing file has
  • encoding mismatch: file has UTF-16BE BOM
  • encoding mismatch: file has UTF-16LE BOM
  • encoding must be a string, code page number, or nil
  • expected a byte string
  • invalid UTF-16 byte length
  • invalid Windows code page
  • string is too large
  • text cannot be represented in Windows code page
  • unsupported Windows code page
  • unsupported encoding:
  • Unsupported file opening mode
  • NUL bytes are not allowed in the string
  • The path is occupied by an object that is not a folder:
  • A nonempty path is required
  • A UTF-8 string is required
  • A UTF-8 string with no NUL bytes is required

Example

local fs = require('fs')
local result, err, code = fs.FileAppend('пример.txt', 'строка')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)
local fs = require('fs')
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = fs.FileWrite('append.txt', 'abc')
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = fs.FileAppend('append.txt', 'def')
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = fs.FileRead('append.txt') == 'abcdef'
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end
fs.FileAppendLine
fs.FileAppendLine(path, text, [encoding], [allow_lossy])
Purpose

Add a logical string to the end; if there is no file, create it.

Description

Add a logical string to the end; if there is no file, create it.

BOM saves an existing file and has a final string translation. Unlike FileAppend, it adds a separator between the lines if necessary.

Difference with fs.FileAppend: adds a separate logical string. If the file contains abc, the addition of def gives abc\r\ndef. Uses the first separator found in the file, and if it is not, CRLF. The presence of the final separator is saved: from abc\n you get abc\ndef\n. The text prohibits CR and LF.

In fs 6.12.2, the presence of a final separator is saved for non-empty text. Empty added string always receives a separator to increase the number of logical rows; the file style or CRLF is used. When creating a new file with a blank line, CRLF is written (with BOM according to encoding).

Parameters
path
UTF-8 path. Relative paths are resolved against the process's current working directory.
text
String. Use UTF-8 with text APIs. See the function description for the meaning and default value.
encoding optional
nil/UTF-8, UTF-8-BOM, UTF-16LE/BE, BINARY, ANSI/ACP, OEM/OEMCP, CP1251/Windows-1251 or a numerical code page. Default: "UTF-8".
allow_lossy optional
boolean: false/nil prohibits irreversible substitution when encoding; true permits. Default: false prohibits loss-of-character conversion.
Returns

true or nil, message[,code].

Error handling

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

Purpose

Description

Insert a line before line_number, moving the rest.

1..FileLineCount+1 is allowed; the original file must exist, saves BOM and the file-selected string translation style.

boolean: false/nil prohibits irreversible substitution when encoding; true permits. Default: false prohibits loss-of-character conversion.

Purpose

The entire file is loaded into memory. Result - row table without CR/LF; recognized CRLF, LF and CR. It is not a streaming iterator. Speed advantage over io.lines() is not guaranteed.

Logical strings are separated by CRLF, LF or single CR; separators are allowed to mix. The final line translation does not create an additional empty string. It opens and closes the file itself. Unlike fs.FileReadLine, it returns the table of all rows, not the iterator. Both functions accept path and optional encoding.

Purpose

Set aside a separate temporary directory for intermediate files.

Description

Creates a new empty folder in the Windows temporary directory and returns its absolute path to UTF-8. When the name matches, a new one is selected. When the name matches, it returns nil, message[, code].

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

The absolute path of the new empty folder in UTF-8.

Error handling

If you refuse, it's nil, message[, code]. The match to an existing name is processed by selecting a new name.

Example

local fs = require("fs")
local folder, err, code = fs.TempDirCreate()
if not folder then print(err, code); return end
