fs.FileReadLine
fs.FileReadLine(path, [encoding])
Purpose

Get an iterator for the line cycle for.

Description

The mode depends on the encoding argument: without encoding, return io.lines(path) is executed; with explicitly specified encoding, Framework reading is used.

After validating the required path, returns the native io.lines iterator. The call performs no UTF-8 validation, transcoding, or special BOM handling. LuaJIT's native text-mode rules apply for line endings and errors.

FrameWork uses the Unicode Windows API for paths, returns UTF-8 text, and recognizes CRLF, LF, and bare CR. It validates UTF-8 and UTF-16 and rejects NUL in text modes. In Unicode modes, it skips a matching BOM only at the start of the file and rejects an incompatible BOM. With an explicit Windows code page, all bytes are treated as data. Encoding detection is not automatic.

The entire file is not loaded into memory. The framework stores the position in the 64 KB buffer and collects fragments only when a line crosses the block boundary. For any encoding, it reads one line; an empty file does not produce strings, the final separator does not create an additional empty string.

PropertiesNo encodingWith explicit encoding
ImplementationDirect call io.linesReading the Framework
Encoding and BOMWithout transcoding and special processing BOMText is converted to UTF-8; BOM is processed into UTF-8/UTF-16
SeparatorsNative text mode LuaJITCRLF, LF and CR
Unicode pathsDepends on the LuaJIT buildUTF-8 via Unicode WinAPI
Path to fileMandatory.Mandatory.

Mistakes: is thrown away as Lua errors. To handle errors, use pcall around the entire loop. The file closes automatically when EOF. The Framework also closes it when read error; the native mode fully follows io.lines. FileReadLine only works with files; there is no reading of standard input.

In the event of a break or error in the loop body, immediate closure of the file is not guaranteed; release occurs after the iterator becomes unavailable to the garbage collector.

For the entire row table, use fs.FileReadLines(path, [encoding]) immediately. It has UTF-8 as its default encoding; it always runs through the Framework.

For streaming read without exception, use fs.FileLinesOpen and the explicit Next() call.

Parameters
path
Mandatory non-empty string: file path without NUL. Missing path, nil, empty string and incorrect type cause error in both modes. For Framework, the path is transmitted to UTF-8; native Unicode path support depends on LuaJIT build.
encoding optional
Passing nil or omitting the argument calls io.lines directly. Explicit UTF-8, UTF-8-BOM, UTF-16LE/BE, CP1251/Windows-1251, ANSI/ACP, OEM/OEMCP, or a supported Windows code page number enables FrameWork processing. BINARY enables FrameWork processing without transcoding and permits NUL. FrameWork does not support UTF-32, stateful encodings, or code pages without ASCII CR/LF.
Returns

Iterator function: Call the iterator produces a string, and EOF - nil. Open/read/close errors cause the exclusion of Lua. Without encoding, io.lines(path) is used; with encoding, the internal managed reader.

Error handling

Lua exceptions when opening, reading, line conversion, and closing. They need to be intercepted by pcall/xpcall around the opening and all the bypass. To return errors without exception, use fs.FileLinesOpen and check each Next(). There is no third code return here.

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

Purpose

Description

Walks a directory tree without collecting the entire result in memory. The callback receives absolute_path, kind, size, user_data, and info. kind is "file" or "directory", a directory has size 0, and info is FileGetInfo metadata. Return 1 to continue, 2 to skip a directory’s contents, or 0 to stop. The function returns true on completion, false when stopped, or nil and an error message on failure, including callback failures. The mask filters files only. The exclude option takes | separated directory-name patterns at any depth. The callback skips the root and excluded directories. The root cannot be a reparse point, and the traversal does not descend into reparse-point directories. The order is unspecified. Memory use depends on the name lists at active levels.

callback
Lua is an event or progress processing function.
pattern optional
Name template for file selection. By default, "*".
exclude optional
Exception templates for skipping matching paths. By default, "".
user_data optional
The Lua value transmitted to the processor as user data.

true after complete bypass, false after stop by handler, nil, message.

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CloseHandle
  • CreateFileW (stat)
  • Directory walk callback
  • FindClose
  • FindFirstFileW
  • FindNextFileW
  • GetFileInformationByHandle
  • GetFullPathNameW
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • absolute path component is only allowed first
  • callback must be a function
  • callback must return 0 (stop), 1 (continue), or 2 (skip)
  • invalid pattern or exclusions
  • path component must be a string
  • root must be a non-reparse directory
  • NUL bytes are not allowed in the string
  • A nonempty path is required
  • A UTF-8 string is required
  • A UTF-8 string with no NUL bytes is required
  • This object is not a folder:

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 31. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local fs = require('fs')
local result, err, code = fs.DirWalk('Данные', function() return 1 end)
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

fs.FileFindLines
fs.FileFindLines(path, needle, [ignore_case=false], [start_line=1], [max_matches=0])
Purpose

Find the lines of the file containing the specified fragment.

Description

Streams a literal search over UTF-8 lines. Returns a table of {number, column, column_codepoint, text} records, one per matching line. column is a 1-based UTF-16 code-unit position, as in PureBasic. column_codepoint is a 1-based Unicode code-point position and counts a surrogate pair as one code point. Byte and grapheme positions are different measures. ignore_case=true performs a case-insensitive Windows ordinal comparison. Empty lines are skipped when searching for nonempty text. An empty needle returns nil, "search text must not be empty". max_matches=0 means no limit. On error, returns nil and an error message.

path, needle, [ignore_case=false], [start_line=1], [max_matches=0]. Arguments in square brackets are optional; default values are indicated in the signature. Paths are transmitted by UTF-8 strings.

Mistakes: nil,message[,code], unless otherwise specified. Modification operations return true if successful. Check nil separately from false.

Parameters
path
Windows path in UTF-8. Relative paths are resolved against the process's current working directory.
needle
A line to be found in the text.
ignore_case optional
Enables case-insensitive comparison. Defaults to false.
start_line optional
The number of the first line to be checked, starting with 1. By default, 1.
max_matches optional
Coincidence limit. 0 removes limit. By default, 0.
Returns

A set of matches to the fields number, column, column_codepoint, text. If there are no matches, the table is blank. If there is an error, nil, message.

fs.DirWatchNext
fs.DirWatchNext(watcher, [timeout=0])
Purpose

Receive one subsequent notification of a change in the folder, which is monitored through DirWatchOpen.

Description

Returns the next change notification from a directory watch opened by DirWatchOpen. Notifications report file or directory creation, deletion, modification, or renaming. Reading a notification does not change the directory.

Once you've completed your observation, call DirWatchClose. Error code 1022 means you've lost notifications: the folder's state needs to be re-routed. After an error about a broken watcher, close it and recreate it.

Sequential calls retrieve accumulated events in order of receipt. When you overflow the buffer, re-list the contents of the directory.

Parameters
watcher
The object returned by fs.DirWatchOpen(path, [recursive], [filter]).
timeout optional
Integer 0 to 60,000: maximum wait in milliseconds; default 0 is to check the queue and return immediately; if there is an event, the queue returns immediately.
Returns
  • Table {action, name, full_path} - received event.
  • false: No progress has been made during the waiting period.
  • nil, message[, code] is a mistake.

name is the name or relative path from the observed folder, in UTF-8. full_path is the full path. action is the action number:

actionMeaning.
1 / fs.watchActions.addedFile or folder created
2 / fs.watchActions.removedFile or folder deleted
3 / fs.watchActions.modifiedObject changed.
4 / fs.watchActions.renamed_oldOld name when renaming
5 / fs.watchActions.renamed_newNew name when renaming

The renaming gives out separate notifications with the old and the new name. The types of changes being tracked are set by the filter in DirWatchOpen. The notifications can be repeated; they are not a ready-made log of all file operations.

Notification table with action, name and full_path fields. false, if there are no notifications by the end of the wait. If there is an error, nil, message and, when available, code. Code 1022 means loss of events.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Read, write, close, and traversal failures may return the original Win32 error code. Recursive operations may make partial changes before failing. Automatic rollback is not guaranteed. Check the code separately from the message.

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • GetOverlappedResult
  • absolute path component is only allowed first
  • directory events lost; enumerate the directory again
  • malformed directory event
  • path component must be a string
  • timeout must be 0..60000 milliseconds
  • watcher has failed; close and reopen it
  • watcher is closed or invalid

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 1022. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument. The internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local fs = require('fs')
local watcher, sampleError, sampleCode = fs.DirWatchOpen('C:/Data')
if not watcher then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local event, err, code = fs.DirWatchNext(watcher, 1000)
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = fs.DirWatchClose(watcher)
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
if event == nil then
    error(err)
elseif event == false then
    print('За секунду изменений не поступило')
else
    print(event.action, event.name, event.full_path)
end

local fs = require('fs')

zip - ZIP: packaging and unpacking 3
zip.Create
zip.Create(source, archive[, overwrite[, mode[, files]]])
Purpose

Pack the file or directory in ZIP and select the required entries if necessary.

Description

Creates ZIP from a single file or folder, saves its name, nested folders, and empty folders, and writes it under its own name.

overwrite is boolean (false default); mode is "exclude" or "include"; files is a string array in the fifth argument. Without mode and files, everything is packaged.

exclude: files contain exception templates; by default {}. include: source must be a folder, files a non-empty array of relative files/folders without templates. Selected folders are included as a whole, intersections do not create duplicates. Paths are saved inside the original root folder.

Returns true or nil, message [, code PowerShell]. The previous archive is saved in case of packaging error. source and parent folder of archive must exist. Requirements and limitations of the zip module.

Paths and templates are transmitted to Windows PowerShell 5.1 in the JSON file (UTF-8). Apostrophes and typographical quotation marks in the names are saved. Success returns after confirmation of the completion of the operation with a script.

Parameters
source
The UTF-8 path to the source file or directory.
archive
The UTF-8 path to the ZIP archive.
overwrite optional
true allows you to overwrite an existing archive. By default, false.
mode optional
"exclude" excludes matches, "include" leaves only the selected.
files optional
In exclude mode, you have an array of names, paths, and exclusion patterns. Include mode, you have a non-empty array of exact relative paths without patterns.
Returns

true is successful. If it fails, nil, message, and if PowerShell fails, its exit code.

Error handling

zip.Extract
zip.Extract(archive, destination [, options])
Purpose

Extract all content or selected files from ZIP.

Description

Unpacks all of ZIP or selected entries into the destination folder. Paths are saved relative to the root of the archive. Folders are created as needed.

  • include is a string array. Without this option, all records are selected. The empty array does not select any records.
  • exclude is a string array. Matches are removed from the include sample. There are no default exceptions.
  • overwrite is a Boolean value, by default false. With true, existing files are replaced. With false, conflict with an existing file causes an error.

The exact names and separator templates are from the root of ZIP. The final / means the folder along with all the content, even if there is no separate entry for the folder in ZIP. A template without separators, such as *.log, is compared to a name at any depth. * means zero or more characters, ? means one character. Templates do not cross the boundaries of the folders. A non-register comparison is taken. The paths take / and \.

Before writing, the paths of selected records, duplicates, file and folder conflicts, symbolic links and reprocessing points along the destination path are checked. CRC32 and the size of each file are checked before saving it. The file changes time is saved. If the previously extracted files are mistaken, the previously extracted files remain on the disk.

Paths and templates are transmitted to Windows PowerShell 5.1 in the JSON file (UTF-8). Apostrophes and typographical quotation marks in the names are saved. Success returns after confirmation of the completion of the operation with a script.

Parameters
archive
The UTF-8 path to the ZIP archive.
destination
The UTF-8 path to the unpacking catalogue.
options optional
Settings table. include selects records, exclude skips them, overwrite allows you to replace existing files.
Returns

true is successful. An empty sample is considered successful and does not create a destination folder. If you fail, you return nil, the message and, if PowerShell ended with an error, its exit code.

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Open the SQLite file or the base :memory:.

Description

Opens the SQLite file or base :memory:. readOnly and busyTimeoutMs options. System winsqlite3.dll is required.

Method of return object: db:Exec(sql[, params]).

Method of return object: db:Query(sql[, params]).

Method of return object: db:Close().

Parameters
path
The UTF-8 path to the base file or ":memory:" for the base in memory.
opts optional
The database settings table. readOnly includes read mode, busyTimeoutMs sets lock waiting.
Returns

Database object. In case of error, nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The third result is SQLite, not Win32: for example, 21 for an incorrect/closed database, 20 for an unsupported parameter type, 25 for a mismatch in the number of parameters. Checks to SQLite can return a message without a code. Exec can successfully return 0.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • GetSystemDirectoryW failed
  • Could not load the library
  • Wrong parameter type
  • Inadmissible value of busyTimeoutMs
  • Unacceptable path to SQLite database
  • Unknown parameter
  • NUL bytes are not allowed in the string
  • Parameters should be a table.
  • A nonempty path is required
  • A UTF-8 string is required

Example

local sqlite = require('sqlite')
local result, err, code = sqlite.Open(':memory:')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)
sqlite.Exec
sqlite.Exec(db, sql [, params])
Purpose

Change the data or database schema of a single SQL command.

Description

Performs one SQL expression and returns the number of lines changed.

After a single expression, space characters are allowed. When a second expression is detected, the call returns the error before the first one is executed.

Parameters
db
Open connection obtained via sqlite.Open.
sql
One SQL command. Use placeholders for parameters.
params optional
sqlite.NULL stands for SQL NULL.
Returns

A whole number of lines changed. In case of error, nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The third result is SQLite, not Win32: for example, 21 for an incorrect/closed database, 20 for an unsupported parameter type, 25 for a mismatch in the number of parameters. Checks to SQLite can return a message without a code. Exec can successfully return 0.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • SQL parameter count mismatch
  • SQLite database is closed or invalid
  • duplicate column name; use SQL aliases
  • expected one SQL statement
  • expected positional parameters array
  • only one SQL statement is allowed
  • unsupported SQLite parameter at index
  • SQL should be an array.
  • SQL string required in UTF-8 without zero byte
  • must be a string
  • invalid UTF-8 at byte
  • unexpected end of string

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 21, 25. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument. The internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local sqlite = require('sqlite')
local result, err, code = sqlite.Exec(db, 'CREATE TABLE settings (value TEXT)')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

db:Exec
db:Exec(sql[, params])
Purpose

Execute a command to change data or structure through an open connection.

Description

Prepares one SQL expression, connects parameters and executes it.

db:Exec(sql[, params])

Receive the object through sqlite.Open(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters
sql
One SQL command. Use placeholders for parameters.
params optional
sqlite.NULL stands for SQL NULL.
Returns

The number of lines changed, including 0, does not return SELECT strings.

Error handling

sqlite.Exec(db, sql, params). nil, message[, SQLiteCode]; closed/incorrect database: 21; parameter mismatch: 25; unsupported parameter: 20. SQL/options may not have code.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local sqlite = require("sqlite")
local db, err, code = sqlite.Open(":memory:")
if db == nil then print(err, code); return end
local result, err, code = db:Exec("CREATE TABLE items (name TEXT)")
if result == nil then print(err, code) else print(result) end
db:Close()
db:Query
db:Query(sql[, params])
Purpose

Read data from SQLite via an open connection.

Description

Performs one SQL expression, links parameters and collects rows by column names.

db:Query(sql[, params])

Receive the object through sqlite.Open(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters
sql
One SQL command. Use placeholders for parameters.
params optional
sqlite.NULL stands for SQL NULL.
Returns

Array of rows-tables; empty array is a successful result. SQL NULL is represented by sqlite.NULL.

Error handling

sqlite.Query(db, sql, params). nil, message[, SQLiteCode]; closed/incorrect database: 21; one statement, number/types of parameters and uniqueness of column names are checked.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local sqlite = require("sqlite")
local db, err, code = sqlite.Open(":memory:")
if db == nil then print(err, code); return end
local result, err, code = db:Query("SELECT ? AS name", {"пример"})
if result == nil then print(err, code) else print(result[1].name) end
db:Close()
db:Close
db:Close()
Purpose

Release the SQLite connection at the end of operation.

Description

Closes the connection previously opened via sqlite.Open.

db:Close()

Receive the object through sqlite.Open(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

true after closure, including re-closure of known facility

Error handling

Alias sqlite.Close(db): unknown object - nil, message, 21; failure sqlite3_close_v2 returns the code SQLite. After the success of Exec/Query give 21.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local sqlite = require("sqlite")
local db, err, code = sqlite.Open(":memory:")
if db == nil then print(err, code); return end
local result, err, code = db:Close()
if result == nil then print(err, code) else print(result) end

process.Exec
process.Exec(program, [args], [workingDir], [options])
Purpose

Run EXE with args and get a table of the capture result.

Description

Run EXE with args and get a table of the capture result.

Recommended option for EXE and Argument Array; no interpretation of shell metasymbols without CMD running.

Parameters
program
A non-empty UTF-8 path/name line launched by EXE.
args optional
nil, finished parameter string or sequential array of arguments; the array is screened elementally. Default: nil - without additional arguments.
workingDir optional
UTF-8-path: The relative path is calculated from the current workflow folder. Default: nil is the current workflow folder.
options optional
Options table; the schema is listed for the module and function, it is not an arbitrary libuv table. Default: nil is the standard launch settings.
Returns

{pid, exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, ok}; or nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The non-zero exitCode of the running program does not equal the Failure of the Framework call. RunWait/ExecWait timeout uses the third position for PID. RunCapture uses the fifth timedOut, and Exec/ExecShell uses the timedOut field of the table.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CreateFileW(NUL) failed
  • CreatePipe
  • CreateProcessW
  • GetExitCodeProcess failed
  • PeekNamedPipe failed
  • ReadFile failed
  • SetHandleInformation
  • TerminateProcess failed
  • Unexpected WaitForSingleObject result after timeout:
  • Unexpected WaitForSingleObject result:
  • WaitForSingleObject after timeout failed
  • WaitForSingleObject failed
  • args must be string, table or nil
  • command line is not valid UTF-8
  • commandLine must be a non-empty string
  • cwd is not valid UTF-8
  • options must be a table or nil
  • options must be string, table or nil
  • program must be a non-empty string
  • target must be a non-empty command line
  • timeout must be zero or greater
  • unsupported Run option:

Example

local process = require('process')
local result, err, code = process.Exec('cmd.exe', {'/d', '/c', 'echo', 'test'})
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

Get the name EXE process.

Description

Get the name EXE process.

Parameters
target optional
Purpose of operation: process - PID/name, window.Win* - HWND/numerical HWND/header/A substrate, shell - path/name of object. Default: nil - current process.
Returns

Line; missing nil; error nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

The non-zero exitCode of the running program does not equal the Failure of the Framework call. RunWait/ExecWait timeout uses the third position for PID. RunCapture uses the fifth timedOut, and Exec/ExecShell uses the timedOut field of the table.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CreateToolhelp32Snapshot failed
  • Process32FirstW failed
  • Process32NextW failed
  • invalid PID
  • process name is not valid UTF-8
  • process target must be PID, process name or nil

Example

local p = require('process')
local pid = require("process").IdGet(); print(p.NameGet(pid))

Purpose

Start the process and wait for its completion.

options.timeout is set in seconds. Timeout does NOT complete the process: PID in the third result is needed for further control.

Parameters
commandLine
Non-empty UTF-8 command string. Shell metasymbols are interpreted only at an explicit CMD/shell call.
options optional
Options table; the schema is listed for the module and function, this is not an arbitrary libuv table. Default: nil are the standard settings for the corresponding function.

exitCode, pid after completion. Timeout is nil, "timeout," pid; third position here is PID, not the error code. Other validated failure is nil, message[, code].

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The non-zero exitCode of the running program does not equal the Failure of the Framework call. RunWait/ExecWait timeout uses the third position for PID. RunCapture uses the fifth timedOut, and Exec/ExecShell uses the timedOut field of the table.

  • CreatePipe
  • CreateProcessW
  • GetExitCodeProcess failed
  • SetHandleInformation
  • WaitForSingleObject failed
  • command line is not valid UTF-8
  • commandLine must be a non-empty string
  • cwd is not valid UTF-8
  • options must be a table or nil

Example

local p = require('process')
local exitCode, detail, third = p.RunWait('cmd.exe /d /c exit /b 7', {hidden=true, timeout=5})

elseif detail == 'timeout' then print('Тайм-аут, PID:', third)
else print(detail, third) end

Purpose

Request the PID process completion code.

Description

Requests PID process completion code. For a still running process, Windows can return STILL_ACTIVE.

WinAPI GetExitCodeProcess

Requests require the right to open a process. Memory metrics use PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ. To confirm the readiness of their process, a named event or response is IPC. Process Security and Access Rights.

Parameters
pid
The numerical identifier of Windows process.
Returns

DWORD: 259 can be either STILL_ACTIVE or the completed process code, or nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The non-zero exitCode of the running program does not equal the Failure of the Framework call. RunWait/ExecWait timeout uses the third position for PID. RunCapture uses the fifth timedOut, and Exec/ExecShell uses the timedOut field of the table.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CloseHandle
  • GetExitCodeProcess
  • Invalid PID
  • OpenProcess

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local process = require("process")
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = process.ExitCodeGet(process.IdGet())
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
print(sampleValue) -- 259 for the current process

process.GetCPUUsage
process.GetCPUUsage(pid [, intervalMs])
Purpose

Measure the load of CPU with the specified process over the interval.

Description

Measures the average load of the processor by a given process per interval.

pid is a numerical process identifier. intervalMs is a whole interval in milliseconds, by default 250. The call awaits completion of the measurement. 100 means loading all the logical processors of the system. One fully occupied logical processor on a system with eight logical processors gives about 12.5.

If the process is terminated during the measurement or access is denied, the error returns.

Parameters
pid
The numerical identifier of Windows process.
intervalMs optional
The interval between the load measurements is in milliseconds. 250 ms by default.
Returns

Number from 0 to 100 or nil, message and code Win32.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The non-zero exitCode of the running program does not equal the Failure of the Framework call. RunWait/ExecWait timeout uses the third position for PID. RunCapture uses the fifth timedOut, and Exec/ExecShell uses the timedOut field of the table.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CloseHandle
  • GetActiveProcessorCount
  • GetProcessTimes
  • Invalid PID
  • OpenProcess
  • Process exited during CPU measurement
  • WaitForSingleObject
  • intervalMs must be positive
  • timeoutMs must be an integer in [0, 4294967294]

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 1067, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument, the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local process = require("process")
local pid = process.IdGet() -- you can specify the PID of another process here.
local usage, sampleError, sampleCode = process.GetCPUUsage(pid, 500)
if not usage then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
print(("%.2f%%"):format(usage))

clipboard.OnChange
clipboard.OnChange(callback)
Purpose

Subscribe to changes in the contents of the clipboard.

Description

Subscribes the processor to Windows notifications about the change of the clipboard.

The handler receives a {sequence = number} table. When working through gui.Run(), the handler is automatically called on the same thread. Hold the subscription while you need it, and call sub:Close() to unsubscribe.

In the console script, sub:Poll(timeoutMs) waits for Windows notification before the specified time. By default, Poll() checks the message queue without waiting. Returns 1 when the handler is called, 0 when there is no change, or nil, message, code when there is an error. The handler receives the current buffer number. Several changes before processing the queue can come in one call.

Method of return object: clipboardSubscription:Poll([timeoutMs]).

Method of return object: clipboardSubscription:Close().

Parameters
callback
Lua is a function that receives a buffer change notification.
Returns

Subscription or nil, message and code Win32.

if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sub, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = clipboard.OnChange(function(event)
    print("Буфер изменён", event.sequence)
end)
if not sub then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
gui.Run()
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = sub:Close()
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end

-- In the console, you can wait for gui.Run() instead of sub:Poll(10000).

Purpose

Read the image from the clipboard.

Description

Reads the clipboard image.

The order of format selection: PNG, CF_DIBV5, CF_DIB. Packed uncompressed DIB with BI_RGB or BI_BITFIELDS. Transparency is maintained when reading PNG. Free the object by :Close() method.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

Object image, nil in the absence of an image or nil, message and code in error.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CloseClipboard
  • CreateWindowExW
  • Decode bitmap
  • Expected nonempty encoded image bytes
  • GdiplusStartup
  • GetClipboardData(image)
  • GlobalLock(clipboard image)
  • Invalid clipboard PNG signature
  • Invalid clipboard image size
  • Invalid or unsupported packed clipboard DIB
  • OpenClipboard
  • RegisterClipboardFormatW(PNG)
  • SHCreateMemStream

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 13, 8, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument, the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local clipboard = require("clipboard")
local pic, err = clipboard.ImageGet()
if pic then
    local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = require("image").Save(pic, "D:\\Temp\\clipboard.png")
    if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
    local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = pic:Close()
    if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
elseif err then
    error(err)
end

Purpose

Description

Serves a subscription and delivers a finished event on the Lua stream.

clipboardSubscription:Poll([timeoutMs])

Receive the object through clipboard.OnChange(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters
timeoutMs optional
The waiting time for a buffer change is in milliseconds.
Returns

Number of notifications delivered (usually 0 or 1); 0 in the absence of an event/timeout. By default, timeoutMs=0.

Error handling

nil, message[, code] in case of an incorrect timeout or wait refusal; closed subscription: 6; exclusion of callback: 31. When automatically delivered through the window manager GUI, Poll refund is not involved: the existing channel writes diagnostics in stderr.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

local clipboard = require("clipboard")

audio.Play
audio.Play(path [, opts])
Purpose

Play the audio file and, if necessary, manage the playback.

Description

Plays the file via MCI. wait=true waits for completion. Returns the object with Close().

When the MCI 304 error occurs, the function tries to open a file with the short name Windows with the same extension. For long paths, you need an accessible short path that accepts MCI.

Method of return object: player:Stop().

Method of return object: player:Close().

Parameters
path
Windows path in UTF-8. Relative paths are resolved against the process's current working directory.
opts optional
Table of playback settings. wait = true is waiting for completion.
Returns

Playable object with Stop and Close. In case of error, nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The code can be HRESULT Core Audio or MCI/Win32; the subsystem is in the text. No default device: HRESULT -2147023728. false from GetMute is the normal result.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Expected UTF-8 string without NUL
  • Invalid audio path
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • Could not load the library
  • Wrong parameter type
  • Unknown parameter
  • NUL bytes are not allowed in the string
  • Parameters should be a table.
  • A nonempty path is required
  • A UTF-8 string is required

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local audio = require('audio')
local result, err, code = audio.Play('пример.wav', {wait=true})
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

local speechHandle, err, code = speech.Speak("Готово", {async = true})

if result == nil then print(err, code) else print(result) end
speechHandle:Close()

speechHandle:Stop()

speechHandle:Stop()

Parameters

No arguments.

true after stoppage; closed or missing handle also gives true.

Error handling

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

speechHandle:Close()
Purpose

Description

Closes the object of voiceover and releases its native resource.

speechHandle:Close()

Receive the object through speech.Speak(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

true after stop and release; re-close also true.

Error handling

There is no separate cleanup bounceback. Close Wait returns nil, message, 6. The object is created only when Speak is async=true.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local speech = require("speech")
local speechHandle, err, code = speech.Speak("Готово", {async = true})

local result, err, code = speechHandle:Close()
if result == nil then print(err, code) else print(result) end

Purpose

Get a readable name of the type of registry value.

Description

Name REG_* by numerical type identifier.

Parameters
valueType
REG_* string/numeric ID or nil for selection by Lua type.
Returns

The line of the name type.

Error handling

The function does not use a separate nil, message for a normal negative result. The return value described above is not a secure boundary for arbitrary erroneous objects or unacceptable FFI arguments.

The numerical status is usually a Windows registry function code. Absence from Read/Exists is different from denial of access. The type of value in a successful Read is not an error code.

Example

local r = require('registry')
print(r.TypeName(4)) -- REG_DWORD
registry.ValueExists
registry.ValueExists(path, [valueName], [view])
Purpose

Check the presence of the named value.

Description

Check the presence of the named value.

nil or empty valueName refers to the default value.

Parameters
path
The path of the Windows Registry key with HKCU/HKLM/HKCR/HKU/HKCC is not the path of the file system.
valueName optional
UTF-8 is the name of the value; nil or "" is the default key value. Default: nil is the default key value. If you pass arguments further, specify nil in this position.
view optional
nil,""native" is the process bit; 32/"32"/"x86" or 64/"64"/"x64" is WOW64 view. Default: nil is the current process bit (native).
Returns

true if there is a value, false if there is no value, nil, err, code if there is an error.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The numerical status is usually a Windows registry function code. Absence from Read/Exists is different from denial of access. The type of value in a successful Read is not an error code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • RegGetValueW
  • RegOpenKeyExW failed
  • invalid registry view
  • registry path cannot be empty
  • registry path cannot be nil
  • registry path is not valid UTF-8
  • unknown registry root:
  • value name is not valid UTF-8

Example

local registry = require('registry')
local result, err, code = registry.ValueExists([[HKCU\Software\Example]], 'Title')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)
registry.Write
registry.Write(path, [valueName], value, [valueType], [view])
Purpose

Create a key if necessary and write down the value.

Description

Create a key if necessary and write down the value.

valueType: REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_DWORD, REG_QWORD, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_BINARY, REG_NONE or numerical ID; nil is selected by Lua type. This is a permanent registry change.

Parameters
path
The path of the Windows Registry key with HKCU/HKLM/HKCR/HKU/HKCC is not the path of the file system.
valueName optional
UTF-8 is the name of the value; nil or "" is the default key value. Default: nil is the default key value. If you pass arguments further, specify nil in this position.
value
Value/data for the operation; acceptable type and format are listed below.
valueType optional
REG_* string/numeric ID or nil to select by Lua type. Default: nil to determine type by value.
view optional
nil,""native" is the process bit; 32/"32"/"x86" or 64/"64"/"x64" is WOW64 view. Default: nil is the current process bit (native).
Returns

true, createdNewKey; error - nil, message, status.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The numerical status is usually a Windows registry function code. Absence from Read/Exists is different from denial of access. The type of value in a successful Read is not an error code.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • QWORD cannot be negative
  • QWORD must contain decimal digits only
  • QWORD requires integer scalar cdata
  • QWORD value is too large
  • REG_MULTI_SZ contains invalid UTF-8
  • REG_MULTI_SZ item contains NUL character
  • REG_MULTI_SZ items must not be empty
  • REG_MULTI_SZ requires a table
  • RegCreateKeyExW failed
  • RegSetValueExW failed
  • binary registry data must be a Lua string
  • invalid QWORD
  • invalid QWORD value
  • invalid REG_DWORD value
  • number is outside exact Lua number range
  • registry path cannot be empty
  • registry path cannot be nil
  • string contains NUL character
  • string is not valid UTF-8
  • unknown registry root:
  • unknown registry value type
  • unsupported registry value type
  • value name is not valid UTF-8

Example

local registry = require('registry')
local result, err, code = registry.Write([[HKCU\Software\Example]], 'Title', 'Пример')
if result == nil then
    if err then print(err) end
    return
end
print(result)

Timer - timers 8
timer.Start
timer.Start([precision])
Purpose

Start measuring the length of the program.

Description

It starts measuring the time interval, for example, before an operation, the speed of which you want to measure, and you get it through timer.Stop().

Precision — nil or finite integer >= 0; this is the number of decimal places as a result of stop. The new start replaces the previous dimension. The module contains one timer.

Parameters
precision optional
Numerical size/quantity/accuracy; integerity and limits are specified in the description. Default: nil - without rounding the result.
Returns

true after the measurement begins. Incorrect accuracy or failure of the meter — nil, message[, code]. A failed repeat Start retains the previous successful measurement.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The meter failure is transmitted as nil, message[, code]. The callback exception is nil, no-empty line, 31. The erroneous callback deletes the timer; the re-cocking failure removes the interval.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • QueryPerformanceCounter
  • The accuracy must be a finite non-negative integer or nil.

Example

local timer = require('timer')
local _, err = timer.Start(2)
if err then print(err); return end
print(timer.Stop())
timer.Stop
timer.Stop([handle])
Purpose

Get the duration of the measurement or cancel the scheduled timer.

Description

Completes the measurement started by timer.Start(), or cancels the scheduled timer if its descriptor is transferred.

After the stop, the timer is reset. The result is in milliseconds, not seconds.

Parameters
handle optional
A descriptor from SetTimeout or SetInterval to cancel the schedule. Without it, the function completes the measurement from Start.
Returns

Without argument, past milliseconds. Unexplained measurement — nil, message; counter failure — nil, message[, code] while maintaining the same measurement. With handle — true when canceled, including repeated; someone else's handle — nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The meter failure is transmitted as nil, message[, code]. The callback exception is nil, no-empty line, 31. The erroneous callback deletes the timer; the re-cocking failure removes the interval.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • QueryPerformanceCounter
  • invalid timer handle
  • timer.Start() was not called

Example

local timer = require('timer')
timer.Start(2); for i = 1, 100000 do local x = i * i end
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = timer.Stop()
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
print(sampleValue, 'ms')

window.MessagePost
window.MessagePost(hwnd, msg[, wParam[, lParam]])
Purpose

Put a message in the window queue and continue working.

Description

Puts a Windows message in the queue of the specified window and immediately returns control, suitable when you do not need a response from the window.

WinAPI PostMessageW

hwnd comes from window.Find or is transmitted by an exact number of window.HwndToNumber. msg - integer 0 to 65,535. wParam and lParam are exact Lua integers and default to 0. The default timeout is 1000 ms. If the window belongs to the calling thread, Windows calls its window procedure directly and ignores the timeout. UIPI can block messages sent to higher-integrity processes. To exchange strings between LuaJIT programs, use ipc. SendMessageTimeoutW

Parameters
hwnd
Descriptor HWND target window. For numerical representation, use window.HwndToNumber.
msg
The integer Windows message code is 0 to 65535.
wParam optional
Entire numerical parameter of the message. Default 0.
lParam optional
Entire numerical parameter of the message. Default 0.
Returns

true, message queued, error nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Legacy window functions often return nil and an error message. See the return values above for missing windows, timeouts, and activation failures. MessagePost, MessageSend, and CopyDataSend preserve available Win32 error codes.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Expected numeric message and integer parameters
  • Invalid HWND
  • PostMessageW
  • invalid HWND
  • window no longer exists

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 1400, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being invoked are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local window = require("window")
local gui = require("gui")
local hwnd, sampleError, sampleCode = gui.WindowClient("Пример", 300, 180)
if not hwnd then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = window.MessagePost(hwnd, 0) -- WM_NULL
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = gui.Close()
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end

The default timeout is 1000 ms. If the window belongs to the calling thread, Windows calls its window procedure directly and ignores the timeout. UIPI can block messages sent to higher-integrity processes. To exchange strings between LuaJIT programs, use ipc. SendMessageTimeoutW

Parameters

Descriptor HWND target window. For numerical representation, use window.HwndToNumber.

The integer Windows message code is 0 to 65535.

Entire numerical parameter of the message. Default 0.
lParam optional
Entire numerical parameter of the message. Default 0.
timeoutMs optional
Maximum latency in milliseconds. 1,000 by default.
Returns

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Legacy window functions often return nil and an error message. See the return values above for missing windows, timeouts, and activation failures. MessagePost, MessageSend, and CopyDataSend preserve available Win32 error codes.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Expected numeric message and integer parameters
  • Invalid HWND
  • SendMessageTimeoutW
  • invalid HWND
  • timeoutMs must be an integer in [0, 4294967294]
  • window no longer exists

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 1400, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being invoked are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local window = require("window")
local gui = require("gui")
local hwnd, sampleError, sampleCode = gui.WindowClient("Пример", 300, 180)
if not hwnd then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local result, err = window.MessageSend(hwnd, 0, 0, 0, 500) -- WM_NULL
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = gui.Close()
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
local sampleValue3, sampleError3, sampleCode3 = result != nil, err
if not sampleValue3 then print(sampleError3 or "Operation failed", sampleCode3); return end
print(result)
window.CopyDataSend
window.CopyDataSend(hwnd, bytes[, dataId[, timeoutMs[, senderHwnd]]])
Purpose

Copy binary data into another window via WM_COPYDATA.

Description

Copies binary data to another window via WM_COPYDATA. The receiver window must process this message.

WinAPI SendMessageTimeoutW, WM_COPYDATA, COPYDATASTRUCT

hwnd is a window of another process that already accepts WM_COPYDATA. bytes is a string from 0 to 4 MiB with arbitrary bytes. dataId is a number from 0 to 4294967295, by default 0. Identifier assignment and data format are agreed between sender and receiver. timeoutMs by default 1000 ms. senderHwnd is an optional call window. If it is omitted, Windows gets 0 in wParam.

Result 0 usually means that the window procedure rejected or ignored the message.At a timeout, the recipient could have already started processing, so resending can lead to reprocessing.UIPI can prohibit sending.In between processes, Windows copies the structure and bytes to the recipient.WM_COPYDATA · SendMessageTimeoutW

Parameters
hwnd
Descriptor HWND target window. For numerical representation, use window.HwndToNumber.
bytes
Lua binary string. There can be zero bytes inside.
dataId optional
Integer identifier of transmitted data. Default 0.
timeoutMs optional
Maximum latency in milliseconds. 1,000 by default.
senderHwnd optional
Sender window descriptor. Passing sends 0.
Returns

LRESULT receiver windows, including 0.false timeout or nil, message, code error.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Legacy window functions often return nil and an error message. See the return values above for missing windows, timeouts, and activation failures. MessagePost, MessageSend, and CopyDataSend preserve available Win32 error codes.

  • Expected a binary string of up to 4 MiB
  • GetWindowThreadProcessId
  • Invalid HWND

  • dataId must be a DWORD
  • invalid HWND
  • senderHwnd must belong to the calling process
  • timeoutMs must be an integer in [0, 4294967294]

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 1400, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being invoked are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument; the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

print(result, err)

WinAPI, memory and libraries DLL

win_types Types of WinAPI 2
WinAPI types and constants
require("win_types")
Purpose

Use common Windows types and flags for direct calls via FFI.

Description

For what: direct calls to Windows API via LuaJIT FFI. For conventional window and controls, gui is sufficient. Windows x64 and LuaJIT x64 are required.

win_types.lua announces C-types DWORD, BOOL, HANDLE, HWND, WPARAM, LPARAM, POINT, RECT, GUID, FILETIME, SYSTEMTIME and the combinations LARGE_INTEGER, ULARGE_INTEGER. This is a description of the sizes, fields and placement of data in memory; there are no DLL functions and constants here.

win_constants.lua connects win_types and declares 371 numerical constants: WM_* messages, WS_* styles, VK_* keys, file flags, encodings and errors. Both modules return one ffi object. Constants are available through ffi.C, not as global Lua variables. Enum constants are read-only.

If only types are needed, require('win_types') is sufficient. require is executed once; FFI ads are common to the process. Do not re-declar GUID, POINT, RECT and other common structures in your own ffi.cdef. gui and file_dialog in this shipment use the common win_types. The private structures of other modules do not become interchangeable just because of size matching.

DLL functions must be declared separately via ffi.cdef:

QuadPart, LowPart/HighPart, and u.LowPart/u.HighPart share storage. In LARGE_INTEGER, HighPart and QuadPart are signed. In ULARGE_INTEGER, they are unsigned. Keep the cdata and use LL or ULL literals for exact large integers. A Lua number loses precision for integers above 2^53. LuaLS may need a class annotation that inherits from ffi.cdata* for dynamic FFI types.

Combine independent flags via bit.bor, check through bit.band. bit returns a landmark 32-bit number: negative with the senior bit is normal. Positive DWORD value: tonumber(ffi.cast('DWORD', flags)). Do not apply bit to HWND and x64 pointers.

WCHAR is a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit. Convert UTF-8 Lua strings to LPCWSTR before passing them to W-suffixed Windows functions. The file API and gui.WideTextMake normally handle this conversion. The modules leave the global io, os, and ffi.load functions in place. Use ffi.load for an external DLL at a Unicode path.

Full example: Examples/16_winapi_types_constants.lua; named GUI flags - lesson 30. A full explanation is also available in the article "Practice of WinAPI: Types, Flags, Structures and UTF-16" next to the library.

Parameters
module name
Line "win_types." To add named constants, connect "win_constants."
Returns

The win_types and win_constants modules return the same ffi table, rather than a separate operations results manager.

Error handling

Direct ffi.new/cast/cdef/load and Windows calls via ffi have their own contracts. Exceptions to LuaJIT intercept pcall, and read the Win32 code only in accordance with the contract called Windows function.

Example

dofile('C:/Libraries/framework/setup_paths.lua')
local ffi = require('win_constants') -- types will be automatically connected
local bit = require('bit')
local style = bit.bor(ffi.C.WS_CHILD, ffi.C.WS_VISIBLE)
print(bit.tohex(style))
print(ffi.C.WM_CLOSE)
local ffi = require('win_constants')
ffi.cdef[[DWORD __stdcall GetCurrentProcessId(void);]]
local kernel32 = ffi.load('kernel32')
print('PID:', tonumber(kernel32.GetCurrentProcessId()))
local ffi = require('win_types')
local point = ffi.new('POINT', {x=10, y=20})
print(tonumber(point.x), tonumber(point.y))
local size = ffi.new('ULARGE_INTEGER', {QuadPart=ffi.new("uint64_t", 4294967297)})
print(tonumber(size.LowPart))    -- 1
print(tonumber(size.u.HighPart)) -- 1
WinAPI Practice: Types, Flags, Structures and UTF-16
Практика WinAPI: типы, флаги, структуры и UTF-16
Purpose

Prepare UTF-16 structures, flags and strings for WinAPI.

Description

win_types.lua and win_constants.lua you need to work directly with Windows API via LuaJIT FFI. guiIt is not necessary to connect the constants separately. Windows x64 and LuaJIT x64 are required.

  • win_types.lua announces C-types: DWORD, BOOL, HANDLE, HWND, WPARAM, LPARAM, POINT, RECT, GUID, FILETIME, SYSTEMTIME, and the LARGE_INTEGER, ULARGE_INTEGER combinations. The types describe the size, fields, and placement of data in memory. There are no DLL functions and constants in this module.
  • win_constants.lua connects win_types and announces 371 numerical constants: WM_* messages, WS_* styles, VK_* virtual keys, file flags, encodings, errors and other values of Win32. The named constant helps to understand the code without looking for values like 0x50000000 in the headers Windows.
  • Both modules return the same object ffi. The constants are available through ffi.C, not as global Lua variables. These are C enum constants; you can't assign new values to them. FFI ads are common to the process, and require loads the module once.

If only types are enough, use require("win_types"). If you want both types and constants, require("win_constants") is enough.

Combine independent flags via bit.bor, check the flag through bit.band. The bit module returns a landmark 32-bit result: a negative number with a higher bit set is normal for DWORD flags. If you need to get a positive number, use tonumber(ffi.cast('DWORD', flags)). Do not apply 32-bit bit operations to HWND and x64 pointers.

Types and constants do not declare DLL functions. Declare the desired function through ffi.cdef, then download the system DLL. An example can be performed after setup_paths.lua:

Do not re-copy the definitions of GUID, POINT, RECT and other common structures into your own ffi.cdef: use the types from win_types. The gui and file_dialog modules in this supply use common definitions. Typed pointers to the private structures of other modules do not automatically become interchangeable just because of size matching.

QuadPartfield LowPart/HighPart and u.LowPart/u.HighPart they use a single memory. LARGE_INTEGER field HighPart and QuadPart signifier ULARGE_INTEGER Store large 64-bit values like cdata and specify exact suffixed literals. LL/ULL: Lua number loses accuracy for integers greater than 2^53. If Lua Language Server does not recognize dynamic FFI-type fields, give an annotation of the class with inheritance from ffi.cdata*This is a tip to the editor, not a change in C memory.

WCHAR - one 16-bit UTF-16 element. Lua string UTF-8 is not LPCWSTR; text WinAPI functions with W suffix require conversion. Paths and text operations are usually more convenient ready-made functions. fileAnd in GUI -- gui.WideTextMakeNew modules don't replace globally io, os or ffi.loadFor external DLL by Unicode Path, use ffi.load.

Ready-made stand-alone example: Examples/16_winapi_types_constants.lua. The use of constants in native GUI is shown in lesson 30.

Parameters

No additional arguments.

Returns

Ffi table with declared Win32 types. Type/descriptor values remain cdata.

Error handling

FFI does not end up in the nil/message Framework. Type description, conversion, and unknown character errors can throw out Lua exceptions; an erroneous raw pointer cannot be made secure by a single pcall.

Example

dofile('C:/Libraries/framework/setup_paths.lua')
local ffi = require('win_constants')
local bit = require('bit')
local style = bit.bor(ffi.C.WS_CHILD, ffi.C.WS_VISIBLE)
print('Стиль контрола:', bit.tohex(style))
print('Сообщение WM_CLOSE:', ffi.C.WM_CLOSE)
local ffi = require('win_constants')
ffi.cdef[[
    DWORD __stdcall GetCurrentProcessId(void);
]]
local kernel32 = ffi.load('kernel32')
print('PID:', tonumber(kernel32.GetCurrentProcessId()))
local ffi = require('win_types')
local point = ffi.new('POINT', { x = 10, y = 20 })
print('Координаты:', tonumber(point.x), tonumber(point.y))
local size = ffi.new('ULARGE_INTEGER', { QuadPart = ffi.new("uint64_t", 4294967297) })
print('Младшие 32 бита:', tonumber(size.LowPart))  -- 1
print('Старшие 32 бита:', tonumber(size.u.HighPart)) -- 1
win_constants is the WinAPI constant. 1
win_constants is a constant called WinAPI.
require("win_constants")
Purpose

Connect named Windows constants for calls via FFI.

Description

It loads win_types and declares named constants in the general FFI space. Returns ffi; values are available through ffi.C. This is not a separate table of numerical flags.

The constant sets and structures are described in the win_types section. Do not repeat the general ffi.cdef ads in your code.

Parameters
module name
Line "win_constants."
Returns

Table LuaJIT ffi; constants declared via FFI and read as ffi.C.CONSTANT.

Error handling

ffi.cdef and unknown character failures are exceptions to LuaJIT. These features do not automatically receive the nil, message, code Framework contract.

Example

local ffi = require("win_constants")
local bit = require("bit")
local style = bit.bor(ffi.C.WS_CHILD, ffi.C.WS_VISIBLE)
print(bit.tohex(style))
print(ffi.C.WM_CLOSE)
cstring_buffer - C-row buffer 3
buffer:Set

Purpose

Replace the text in the buffer already allocated.

Description

Write bytes to the buffer and put the final NUL.

buffer:Set(text)

Receive the object through cstring_buffer.New(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters
text
A line that needs to be placed in a buffer.
Returns

Same buffer object; a string of bytes with the NUL ending is written.

Error handling

nil, message, if text is not a string, contains NUL or #text >= size. size includes space for the terminator; UTF-8 is not checked.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local cstring_buffer = require("cstring_buffer")
local buffer, err, code = cstring_buffer.New(32)
if buffer == nil then print(err, code); return end
local result, err, code = buffer:Set("Привет")
if result == nil then print(err, code); return end
print(buffer:ToString()) -- Hey.
buffer:ToString
buffer:ToString()
Purpose

Get a Lua line from a C buffer.

Description

Copies buffer bytes up to the first NUL.

buffer:ToString()

Receive the object through cstring_buffer.New(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

The string of bytes up to the first NUL is within size.

Error handling

nil, message, if there is no NUL within the buffer, does not perform unlimited searches outside of the buffer memory.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local cstring_buffer = require("cstring_buffer")
local buffer, err, code = cstring_buffer.New(32)
if buffer == nil then print(err, code); return end
local updated, err, code = buffer:Set("Привет")

print(result)
cstring_buffer.New
cstring_buffer.New(size)
Purpose

Create a fixed char buffer for the C-line.

Description

Create a fixed char buffer for the C-line.

Size - bytes with the final NUL, not the number of characters and not WCHAR.

Byte buffer C-line. Capacity includes the final NUL. set() prohibits built-in NUL and overflow; tostring() checks for NUL within the buffer. UTF-8 is not checked.

This module creates only char[]: byte C-strings with NUL. This is not WCHAR[] nor a UTF-16 buffer. Do not pass it as the output buffer of Windows functions with the W suffix; for these, separately select WCHAR[] of the desired capacity in the UTF-16 elements.

The method of tostring() searches for NUL within the container and copies only the string. If the C code overwrote NUL and there is no terminator in the entire buffer, nil, message returns.

Method of return object: buffer:Set(text).

Method of return object: buffer:ToString().

Parameters
size
Buffer capacity in bytes.
Returns

An object with data, size and Set(text), ToString() fields includes the final NUL. If the allocation is incorrectly sized or failed, nil, message.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil and an error message. A third return value with a numeric error code is optional.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • buffer is not NUL-terminated
  • buffer size must be an integer from 1 to 2147483647
  • embedded NUL is not allowed in a C string
  • expected a string
  • string does not fit in buffer (including NUL)

Example

local cstring_buffer = require('cstring_buffer')
local b, sampleError, sampleCode = cstring_buffer.New(64)
if not b then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = b:Set('Привет')
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end
print(b:ToString())

Extension of WinAPI

ipc – Data exchange between processes 16
ipc.PipeServerCreate
ipc.PipeServerCreate(name[, options])
Purpose

Create a server side of a named channel to exchange messages between processes.

Description

Creates the server side of the named channel to exchange messages between processes. To wait for the client, then call PipeAccept.

WinAPI CreateNamedPipeW

The channel works in binary mode. The message consists of the length of uint32 little-endian and the specified number of bytes. Empty messages and NUL within the message are permissible. The server object serves one client at a time. For parallel clients, you can create multiple instances with the same name and agreed parameters.

Server options.

  • maxMessageBytes sets the limit in both directions. By default, 4 MiB. The client created through PipeConnect uses its fixed limit of 4 MiB.
  • bufferBytes sets the size of each NPFS buffer, 64 KiB by default. Windows can adjust it. The message can be larger than the buffer.
  • localOnly is the default true, which includes PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS. Client API always opens the local name \\.\pipe\<name>. localOnly=false allows the server to receive connections from remote native clients within ACL Windows.
  • timeoutMs sets the default timeout for server operations to 5000 ms. An explicit timeout ranges from 0 to 4294967294 ms. Zero checks immediately. The client defaults to 5000 ms. If the pipe name has not been created yet, the client waits briefly between attempts. If all instances are busy, it uses WaitNamedPipeW.

By default, ACL allows access to the current user and SYSTEM. PID can be used for diagnostics. The request will be answered to confirm application readiness. After the connection is broken, the read or write returns the Windows error. When the write timeout, read timeout after the message begins or exceeds the limit, the received connection breaks so that the next call receives the whole message. The server can be reused, the client needs to connect again. If the byteers are not yet read, the reading can be repeated. Before the memory is released, the operation is completed in NPFS204Q. CreateNamedPipeW · CancelIoEx

If the client closes the connection before the PipeAccept call, the function returns the Win32 232 error.The instance is reset, and the next PipeAccept call can receive another client.

A successful PipeWrite means writing to a channel. PipeDisconnect discards unread data. To confirm delivery, wait for a customer response with a predetermined timeout before shutting down or shutting down the server, as in Examples 25 and 26.

From the root of the kit in two CMD windows.

The test versions of Tests\ipc_server.lua and Tests\ipc_client.lua take the same channel name as the first argument and further check the echoes of empty, binary and large messages.

Parameters
name
The name of the channel, buffer, or recipient in UTF-8. Use the same name for the other party.
options optional
Table of parameters maxMessageBytes, bufferBytes, timeoutMs and localOnly.
Returns

The server object. name - short name UTF-8 without slashes, along with a prefix of up to 255 units of UTF-16. nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

PipeAccept/PipeConnect/PipeRead/PipeWrite - false. Closed/fault object and Win32 failures are returned separately. Pipe messages are binary: an empty string cannot be considered a failure.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • ConvertSidToStringSidW
  • ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW
  • CreateEventW
  • CreateNamedPipeW
  • Expected UTF-8 string without NUL
  • Expected a short logical name without slashes
  • Expected pipe options table
  • GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)
  • Invalid pipe options
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • Object name exceeds 255 UTF-16 units
  • OpenProcessToken
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • timeoutMs must be an integer in [0, 4294967294]
  • Could not load the library

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 206, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument, the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local ipc = require("ipc")
local server, err, code = ipc.PipeServerCreate("FrameWork.Reference.Pipe")
if server == nil then print(err, code); return end
print("Сервер создан")
ipc.PipeClose(server)

For the complete IPC example, see 25_ipc_server.lua and 26_ipc_client.lua.

  • localOnly is the default true, which includes PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS. Client API always opens the local name \\.\pipe\<name>. localOnly=false allows the server to receive connections from remote native clients within ACL Windows.
  • timeoutMs sets the default timeout for server operations to 5000 ms. An explicit timeout ranges from 0 to 4294967294 ms. Zero checks immediately. The client defaults to 5000 ms. If the pipe name has not been created yet, the client waits briefly between attempts. If all instances are busy, it uses WaitNamedPipeW.

By default, ACL allows access to the current user and SYSTEM. PID can be used for diagnostics. The request will be answered to confirm application readiness. After the connection is broken, the read or write returns the Windows error. When the write timeout, read timeout after the message begins or exceeds the limit, the received connection breaks so that the next call receives the whole message. The server can be reused, the client needs to connect again. If the byteers are not yet read, the reading can be repeated. Before the memory is released, the operation is completed in NPFS204Q. CreateNamedPipeW · CancelIoEx

If the client closes the connection before the PipeAccept call, the function returns the Win32 232 error.The instance is reset, and the next PipeAccept call can receive another client.

Successful PipeWrite means writing to a channel. PipeDisconnect discards unread data. Shutdown also works if the client has already opened the channel and the server has not yet called PipeAccept. To confirm delivery, wait for the client's response with a predetermined timeout before shutting down or closing the server, as in Examples 25 and 26.

From the root of the kit in two CMD windows.

The test versions of Tests\ipc_server.lua and Tests\ipc_client.lua take the same channel name as the first argument and further check the echoes of empty, binary and large messages.

Parameters
server
A server object from ipc.PipeServerCreate.
Returns

true, you can send it back to PipeAccept again, if you make an error, nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

PipeAccept/PipeConnect/PipeRead/PipeWrite - false. Closed/fault object and Win32 failures are returned separately. Pipe messages are binary: an empty string cannot be considered a failure.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • CloseHandle
  • DisconnectNamedPipe
  • Invalid or closed pipe
  • Pipe is disconnected

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 233, 6. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument. The internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local ipc = require("ipc")
local server, err, code = ipc.PipeServerCreate("FrameWork.Reference.Pipe")
if server == nil then print(err, code); return end
print("Run the client in another process")
local connected, acceptError, acceptCode = ipc.PipeAccept(server, 10000)
if not connected then
    print(acceptError or "The client did not connect within 10 seconds", acceptCode)
    ipc.PipeClose(server)
    return
end
local ok, disconnectError = ipc.PipeDisconnect(server)
if not ok then print(disconnectError) end
-- Now you can call PipeAccept again.
ipc.PipeClose(server)

For the complete IPC example, see 25_ipc_server.lua and 26_ipc_client.lua.
