ipc.SharedMemoryCreate
ipc.SharedMemoryCreate(name[, capacity[, timeoutMs]])
Purpose

Allocate a named buffer to transfer one current value between processes.

Description

object, created. capacity — from 1 byte to 64 MiB, by default 1 MiB. When the name and size match opens the existing buffer. At a different size returns the error 183

WinAPI CreateFileMappingW, MapViewOfFile

Named buffer stores one binary string. Write replaces the whole value. Reading returns a copy that can be used after closing. The first value is a blank string. Use Named Pipes for a message queue. To wait for a new record, coordinate the signal using sync.EventSet and sync.EventWait.

Operations with timeoutMs return false if the mutex is not received in time. 5,000 ms default timeout, zero makes an immediate attempt. Names are short UTF-8 lines without slashes. Display and mutex are in the current session Local\ space and are available to the current user and SYSTEM. The buffer is placed in the Windows memory and exists until the last view and descriptor closes.

In the general area, there is a header with a version of the format and a fixed data capacity. Mutex protects initialization, reading and writing. When a writer crashes, the reader gets an error instead of partial data, and the next successful entry restores the buffer. Sharing Files and Memory

From the root of the kit in two CMD windows.

Parameters
name
The name of the channel, buffer, or recipient in UTF-8. Use the same name for the other party.
capacity optional
Buffer capacity from 1 byte to 64 MiB. By default, 1 MiB.
timeoutMs optional
Time-out in milliseconds. 0 sets an immediate check. When you miss, you use a time-out of an object or operation.
Returns

Shared memory object and flag created. false at timeout. If you make an error, nil, message, code.

Purpose

Create a hidden receiver window and register the command handler.

Description

Creates a hidden receiver window and registers the command handler.

One recipient per process. Names are compared without register. When the name is occupied, Win32 183 returns. The handler is called on the stream that called Listen. After Listen, run gui.Run(), as in the full example.

Full script: two-process example.

name
The name of the channel, buffer, or recipient in UTF-8. Use the same name for the other party.

true after registration of the recipient. In case of error - nil, message, code. Code 183 means that the name is taken or the recipient has already started.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The Listen/Post call errors are returned synchronously, and the deletion of the handler of an already received message is recorded to the stderr via an existing secure channel; it does not become a Post result and is not connected to gui.ErrorGet.

Purpose

Send a numerical command to a recipient registered through CommandListen.

Description

Puts the numerical command in the queue of the recipient.

command from 0 to 2147483647. value from −2147483648 to 2147483647, by default 0. true means queuing. If no recipient is found, Win32 1168 returns.

Full script: two-process example.

Parameters
name
The name of the channel, buffer, or recipient in UTF-8. Use the same name for the other party.
command
Integer team number from 0 to 2147483647.
value optional
Integer command argument from −2147483648 to 2147483647. Defaults to 0.
Returns

true, if Windows put the command in a queue, nil, message, code. The 1168 code means no recipient has been found.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The Listen/Post call errors are returned synchronously, and the deletion of the handler of an already received message is recorded to the stderr via an existing secure channel; it does not become a Post result and is not connected to gui.ErrorGet.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • Expected UTF-8 string without NUL
  • Expected a nonempty UTF-8 receiver name
  • Expected a nonnegative 31-bit command and a signed 32-bit value
  • Expected numeric message and integer parameters
  • Invalid HWND
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • PostMessageW
  • Receiver name exceeds 255 UTF-16 units
  • Window IPC receiver not found
  • invalid HWND
  • window no longer exists

In the chain of checks, codes are clearly used: 1168, 1400, 206, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument. The internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local commands = require("ipc")
local sampleValue, sampleError, sampleCode = commands.CommandPost("MyApp.Commands", 1, 42)
if not sampleValue then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end

Sync - Named Events and Mutex 11
sync.EventCreate
sync.EventCreate(name[, manualReset[, initialState]])
Purpose

Create or open a named event by which one process can inform another of its completion or completion.

Description

Creates or opens a named event by which one process can inform another of the readiness or completion of the work.

WinAPI CreateEventW

Names are allowed in the Local\ of the current session, and the same ACL as the ipc is applied.

Timeouts in ms, default 5000."abandoned" means that the trigger stream already owns the mutex and must check the consistency of the data before releasing it.For every successful capture, a separate MutexUnlock is needed.WaitForSingleObject

Parameters
name
The name of the event or mutex in the Local space of the current Windows session.
manualReset optional
true includes manual reset. false or nil selects automatic reset.
initialState optional
true creates a new event in the signal state. By default, false.
Returns

event, created. Both of the default flags are false. If the object already existed, Windows retains its previous type of reset and condition. If the error is nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

A wait timeout returns false without an error. On success, MutexLock can return true, "abandoned" when it acquires an abandoned mutex.

Diagnostic conditions and implementation checks

The following entries describe the conditions and operations that can fail in this function and its internal checks. Message descriptions are in English. The actual text may be localized and may include a path, index, or system detail. Use the numeric code when available for programmatic checks.

  • ConvertSidToStringSidW
  • ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW
  • Event flags must be boolean
  • Expected UTF-8 string without NUL
  • Expected a short logical name without slashes
  • GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)
  • MultiByteToWideChar
  • Object name exceeds 255 UTF-16 units
  • OpenProcessToken
  • WideCharToMultiByte
  • Could not load the library

The chain of checks clearly uses codes: 206, 87. In addition to these, dynamic codes of the subsystem being called are possible; no code is allowed when checking the argument, the internal code can be converted to a standard negative result as described above.

Example

local sync = require("sync")
local name = "Framework example " .. require("process").IdGet()
local event, sampleError, sampleCode = sync.EventCreate(name, true, false)
if not event then print(sampleError or "Operation failed", sampleCode); return end
local sampleValue2, sampleError2, sampleCode2 = sync.EventClose(event)
if not sampleValue2 then print(sampleError2 or "Operation failed", sampleCode2); return end

monitor.ListGet
monitor.ListGet()
Purpose

Use to place a window in the accessible part of the screen.

Description

It lists the monitors and their workspaces. Use them to place a window in the accessible part of the screen.

WinAPI EnumDisplayMonitors, GetMonitorInfoW

Coordinates are taken from the virtual desktop in Win32 pixels, returned to the DPI context of the calling process. They can be negative. Windows can virtualize DPI and coordinates for DPI-unaware and system-aware applications. The identifier is valid until the configuration of the monitors changes. GetDpiForMonitor

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

{id, primary, rect, work, deviceName}. primary — boolean, deviceName — UTF-8. rect and work contain numerical left, top, right, bottom. When mistaken — nil, message, code.

Error handling

http – HTTP, HTTPS and streaming 6
http.Request
http.Request(method, url[, options])
Purpose

Suitable for calling API, when you need to read the answer in memory.

Description

Sends a HTTP request with the selected method, headers and body, suitable for calling API when you need to read the answer in memory.

WinAPI WinHttpOpenRequest, WinHttpSendRequest, WinHttpReceiveResponse, WinHttpReadData

The headers response contains lower case names and value arrays, including for a single header. For example, response.headers["content-type"][1]. Answers 4xx/5xx are returned with their HTTP status. Absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL are accepted for the request, the server name in IDN is encoded via IdnToAscii. The fragment after # is discarded before sending.

  • headers is a {["X-Name"] = "value"} table, body is a string of bytes. WinHTTP shows the length of the body.
  • connectTimeoutMs, sendTimeoutMs, receiveTimeoutMs are positive milliseconds, by default at 15,000 ms. With FwWinHttp64.dll, the wait to complete a shipment is limited to the smaller of 2 * connectTimeoutMs + sendTimeoutMs and receiveTimeoutMs. Headers and each body block are expected to reach receiveTimeoutMs.
  • timeoutMs sets the total network latency limit, from 1 to 2147483647 ms. Upon expiration, nil, message, 12002 returns. For a script, DLL lies next to http.lua, for a packed application next to EXE. Without it, previous calls use system timeouts, and an explicit timeoutMs returns a boot error. The call takes up the call stream. Synchronous operations of the file system can end later than the limit.
  • maxRedirects is 0 to 100, default 10. Auto-junction is valid for GET and HEAD without body and user headers. Otherwise, the original 3xx returns. WinHTTP applies TLS certificate system verification and blocks the transition from HTTPS to HTTP.
  • maxBodyBytes is the response limit in bytes. For Request and Get, the default is 16 MiB, for Download, the default is without a predetermined limit. Exceeding is 223.
  • onProgress(bytesWritten, totalBytes) is called on the Lua stream after the block is written. At unknown length, the second argument is nil. Return false cancels the download with the code 1223. The handler error returns the code 31. In both cases, the previous file is saved.
  • overwrite for Download by default false. The temporary file is created next to the target, written in blocks of 64 KB and renamed after successful completion. The parent directory must exist. Incomplete response and 206 Partial Content are not published as a complete file.

WinHTTP Security Considerations · WinHTTP Option Flags

For answers with the body and known Content-Length, the actual length is checked. When a cliff breaks, code 38 or WinHTTP error is possible.

Parameters
method
HTTP is a string-like method, such as "GET" or "POST".
url
The address is HTTP or HTTPS as a string.
options optional
Table of HTTP query parameters, including titles and timeouts.
Returns

{status, headers, body, finalUrl}. status is the numerical HTTP status, body is the binary string, finalUrl is the final URL. If the error is nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

Purpose

Useful for diagnosing local connection.

Description

It lists network adapters, their addresses and status, useful for diagnosing local connectivity.

WinAPI GetAdaptersAddresses, InetNtopW

AdaptersGet returns for each adapter id (system identifier), name, description, dnsSuffix, ipv4Index and ipv6Index (0 if there is no index for the family), ipv4Metric and ipv6Metric, type (Numerical type of IANA interface), statusCode line status, mtu in bytes, mac format AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF if present, flag dhcpV4 speed transmitBps / receiveBps in bits per second. addresses, dnsServers and gateways - arrays of records {address, family, scopeId}. family it's 4 or 6. scopeId it is available for IPv6 and prefixLength it is added to the interface address when Windows reports the length of the prefix. The indexes may change after the adapter is turned off and re-enabled.

InterfaceStatsGet return index, name, mtu, type, status, statusCodespeed transmitBps and receiveBps, counters receivedBytes / sentBytes, receivedUnicastPackets / sentUnicastPackets, receivedNonUnicastPackets / sentNonUnicastPackets, receivedErrors / sentErrors and receivedDiscards / sentDiscardsCounters and speeds beyond the exact integer Lua are transmitted in decimal lines.

BestRouteGet takes, for example, "127.0.0.1", "::1" or IPv6 with a numerical interface index after %It's back. {index, destinationPrefix, source, nextHop, onLink, metric, protocol}. destinationPrefix - address with a prefix length, source and nextHop - address records, if available. onLink means a route without an intermediate gateway. metric - route metric from Windows, protocol The route is taken from the local routing table.

eventlog.ChannelsGet
eventlog.ChannelsGet()
Purpose

Select Windows channel from the list of registered journals.

Description

Lists the registered channels of Windows magazines to select the channel to read.

WinAPI EvtOpenChannelEnum, EvtNextChannelPath

channel The name of the UTF-8 channel, for example. "Application", "System" name "Microsoft-Windows-…/Operational"Access is subject to Windows channel rights. enabled, classic and full - logical values. type — admin, operational, analytic, debug or unknown. typeCode - Windows source code. isolationCode 0 for Application, 1 for System, or 2 for user isolation. owningPublisher The name of the owner, if available. sizeBytes - size in bytes, recordCount - number of records, oldestRecordNumber - the number of the first record available. lastWriteUtc The time of writing to a log file in UTC.

Read options.

  • query is a XPath filter for that channel. By default, "*", all events.
  • limit is the maximum number of records, from 1 to 1000, by default 50.
  • newestFirst is the default true. false reads from old to new. For Analytic and Debug channels, Windows supports direct order.
  • timeoutMs is a waiting timeout for each portion in EvtNext, by default 5000 ms. At a timeout, already read records and true are returned. Without a timeout, the second result of false. The empty filter result is {}, false.
  • includeXml is the default false. With true, xml is added to the record with the original XML in UTF-8. The total volume of XML result is limited to 16 MiB. Exceeding returns the 223 error.

The recordings are open fields. provider, eventId, qualifiers, level, task, opcode, keywords, recordId, processId, threadId, channel, computer, version, timeUtc and time100nsThe fields missing from the event are lowered. timeUtc iSO 8601 format with seven fractional second characters and suffix Z. time100ns FILETIME time in 100 ns units from 1601-01-01 UTC. 64-bit values that go beyond the range of exact integers Lua are returned by decimal lines.

Windows Event Request · EvtNext · Event properties

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

An array of registered Windows channel names, sorted by name. If mistaken, nil, message, code.

Error handling

On a handled failure, returns nil, message[, code]. The message describes the error. Argument validation and some wrappers may omit the code.

The API error returns separately from the partial timeout result: Read/FileRead returns events, timedOut. code for the present failure refers to Windows Event Log/Win32.

    print(channel)
end

Purpose

Read events from the saved EVTX file without connecting to the source channel.

Description

Reads events from the saved EVTX file without connecting to the source channel.

WinAPI EvtQuery(EvtQueryFilePath), EvtNext, EvtRender

path and destination accept Windows paths in UTF-8. Relative paths are allowed relative to the current working directory. For Export, the destination folder must exist. The query option specifies XPath, by default "*". The empty sample creates the correct EVTX with zero records. The overwrite default option is false. To allow the file replacement, pass {overwrite = true}.

The export is synchronized. The file is first written to a temporary folder next to the destination and moved after successful completion. If the failure occurred before the transfer, the error returns as nil, message, code. If the file has already been published, but Windows refused to delete the empty time folder, true, warning, code returns.

Example

local eventlog = require("eventlog")
local path, sampleError, sampleCode = arg[1], "Передайте путь к существующему EVTX"

Purpose

Description

Stores XPath entries of the specified Windows channel in EVTX.

true after saving a copy of selected records in EVTX

WinAPI EvtExportLog, MoveFileExW

path and destination accept Windows paths in UTF-8. Relative paths are allowed relative to the current working directory. For Export, the destination folder must exist. The query option specifies XPath, by default "*". The empty sample creates the correct EVTX with zero records. The overwrite default option is false. To allow the file replacement, pass {overwrite = true}.

The export is synchronized. The file is first written to a temporary folder next to the destination and moved after successful completion. If the failure occurred before the transfer, the error returns as nil, message, code. If the file has already been published, but Windows refused to delete the empty time folder, true, warning, code returns.

Release of the returned image: imageObject:Close(). After closing, other operations cause a closed object error.

image.DrawText(object, text, x, y [, opts])
Purpose

Add a caption or title to an existing image.

Description

Draws the text of UTF-8 in an open image.

The coordinates x and y define the upper left corner of the area in pixels from the beginning of the image.

  • font is the name of the installed family. By default, GDI+ selects the standard sans-serif family.
  • size is a positive font size in pixels, by default 16. bold and italic include the fonts available in the selected family.
  • color is the color 0xRRGGBB, which is black by default. alpha is opacity from 0 to 255, by default 255. Text is superimposed over the image with transparency in mind.
  • width and height define the size of the area. The lower values extend the area to the right and bottom edges. The text is cropped along its boundaries.
  • align accepts "left", "center" or "right". By default, "left". wrap = false disables automatic line transfer.

imageObject:Close
imageObject:Close()
Purpose

Free up raster image resources.

Description

It closes the image object by performing the same operation as image.Close(object).

imageObject:Close()

Receive the object through image.FromBytes(). The two-point transmits the object to the method automatically.

Parameters

No arguments.

Returns

true after image release, including re-closing.

Error handling

Alias image.Close(object): the wrong object is nil, message, 6; the GDI+ DisposeImage failure returns its code. The other closed image operations give code 6.

The contract applies to objects returned by the named factory. Passing a substitute self or changing an object's internal fields is unsupported.

Example

local image = require("image")
local imageObject, err, code = image.Load("пример.png")
if imageObject == nil then print(err, code); return end
local ok, err, code = imageObject:Close()
if ok == nil then print(err, code); return end
